heuristics.rule: Do not mention visa status or sponsorship needs in the first cold email
heuristics.condition: When you are an international student on OPT or requiring sponsorship and are doing cold outreach...
heuristics.action: Omit visa/sponsorship information from the first email entirely; surface it only when the conversation has developed into a real opportunity
heuristics.because: OP reported this directly and top comment (456 upvotes) corroborated: leading with sponsorship needs triggers rejection before the reader evaluates skills; delaying it until the person is already invested produces better outcomes

decision_factors.factor: SOC Code Selection for PM Roles
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines which prevailing wage schedule applies for H-1B filing; incorrect classification can invalidate the Labor Condition Application
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Default to SOC 11-3021 for tech PM roles; use SOC 11-2021 for growth PM or product marketing manager roles; use SOC 11-1021 for non-tech company PM roles

decision_factors.factor: DOL Wage Level Assignment (Level I–IV) under SOC 11-3021
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Directly determines the number of H-1B lottery entries under the wage-weighted system effective February 2026; also determines LCA compliance
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare offered salary against DOL FLC Data Center prevailing wage thresholds for the specific occupation × location combination; approximate 2024–2025 thresholds vary by metro (e.g., SF Level I ~$170,000, Level IV ~$260,000+; NYC Level I ~$159,000, Level IV ~$245,000+; Austin Level I ~$130,000, Level IV ~$202,000+)

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Prevailing wages differ significantly by metro area; the same role can carry a Level I wage in Austin that would be below Level I in San Francisco
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Use DOL FLC Data Center prevailing wage by metro: SF Bay Area median SOC 11-3021 = $248,400; Seattle = $217,400; NYC = $201,300; Austin = $185,200; national median = $169,510

decision_factors.factor: Work Experience Prior to Management Appointment
decision_factors.why_it_matters: BLS OOH states 3–5 years in subordinate roles is required before typical management appointment; relevant to establishing qualifications for H-1B specialty occupation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Verify petitioner has 3–5 years of relevant subordinate-role experience per BLS OOH standard for SOC 11-3021

decision_factors.why_it_matters: BLS states most Computer and Information Systems Managers have a bachelor's degree in CS, IT, or related field; relevant to specialty occupation determination for H-1B
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm bachelor's degree in CS, IT, or related field; note MBA is increasingly common for senior PM leadership roles per BLS OOH

decision_factors.why_it_matters: SOC 11-3021 employment is distributed across industries; pure tech ('Information' sector) accounts for only 9% of employment, affecting wage benchmarks and petition context
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify employer industry: Professional/scientific/technical services (24%), Finance/insurance (17%), Manufacturing (10%), Information/tech (9%), Government (8%)

decision_factors.why_it_matters: The same dollar value of equity has different real-world value depending on vesting cadence, cliff length, and refresh schedule — quarterly vesting (Meta) provides far higher liquidity than annual cliff structures
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask for the full vesting schedule, whether there are annual refresh grants, and whether the company vests monthly, quarterly, or annually after the cliff; calculate what you would actually receive in years 1 and 2

decision_factors.why_it_matters: The market friction for PM job searches increases measurably after 35 and more sharply after 40 — this changes the urgency, targeting strategy, and timeline planning for any company switch
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Know your current age, calculate years until each threshold, and map planned career moves against those windows explicitly rather than assuming a flat hiring market

decision_factors.factor: Title and scope jump vs. lateral move
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A significantly more senior Canadian role may justify a total comp reduction; a lateral move does not
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare the scope, team size, and title level of the Canadian offer against what you would realistically achieve in the US within 12–18 months

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Title inflation means a 'Senior PM' offer at one company may correspond to a lower level band than the same title at another; the level code determines the compensation band and career progression track
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Request the internal level code explicitly (e.g., L5 at Google, L6 at Amazon, IC5 at Meta) and cross-reference against levels.fyi median for that specific level code

decision_factors.factor: Consumer tech vs. enterprise/regulated industry target
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Age bias is concentrated in consumer tech IC roles and largely absent from enterprise software, regulated industries, and management tracks — the same candidate faces dramatically different market reception depending on sector
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research the PM team composition at target companies (average tenure, age distribution if visible), and assess whether the company's customer base is 18–34 or 35–55

decision_factors.why_it_matters: For some candidates, Canadian permanent residency is the primary goal, which changes the entire comp calculus
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine whether the candidate is actively pursuing PR or has existing status — if PR is the goal, a comp cut is effectively the price of that security

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Equivalent roles pay materially more in NY/SF than Seattle or Austin; a role that appears below market may simply reflect a location adjustment, or a role that appears competitive may be inflated by location
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Filter levels.fyi data by the specific metro area of the role; compare NY/SF comp to Seattle or Austin benchmarks for the same level to isolate the location effect

decision_factors.why_it_matters: PM leaders at 45–55 are common at large companies; senior IC PMs at 50+ are rare in consumer tech — the track you are on determines how long your market viability window extends
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether your recent roles have been adding management scope or deepening IC scope, and whether your target companies have visible examples of senior IC PMs over 45

decision_factors.why_it_matters: RSUs at US public companies are liquid from vest date; equity at Canadian private companies is illiquid and may never pay out
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify whether the company is publicly traded, recently funded, or pre-IPO — then discount equity accordingly

decision_factors.factor: Stock price trajectory of the offering company
decision_factors.why_it_matters: RSU grants are quoted at current stock price but vest over 4 years; a company whose stock declines 40% over the vest period delivers far less than the stated total comp
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate the company's stock performance trajectory, refresh grant policies, and whether the company reprices or issues additional grants during downturns

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Startup and enterprise roles that require specific domain depth (finance, healthcare, logistics) value experience that cannot be quickly replicated — this is the primary counter to age bias for 40+ PMs
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify whether you have 7+ years of accumulated domain knowledge in a regulated or technically specialized area, and whether target companies have a customer relationship moat that requires that depth

decision_factors.why_it_matters: US-parented companies operating in Canada (Amazon, Google, Microsoft) offer RSU compensation that meaningfully closes the Canada–US gap; Canadian-founded companies generally do not
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether the company is a subsidiary of a US public company or a Canadian-founded entity with or without recent funding

decision_factors.factor: Market timing — entry-level vs. senior-level demand
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The current market (2024–2025) is strong for Staff/Principal PM roles but compressed for entry and mid-level; this asymmetry changes negotiation leverage and job availability depending on where you are in your career
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess your current level against where hiring demand is concentrated; if you are at Senior+ with 7–10 years at quality companies, leverage is high; if you are APM or early PM, supply exceeds demand

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Prevention of age discrimination effects is more effective than legal remedy — a strong network enables referral-based hiring that bypasses ATS filters, junior interviewer bias, and culture-fit proxies
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess how many hiring decision-makers (not just peers) are in your active network, and whether you have relationships that would yield warm introductions at target companies

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Ontario marginal tax at $150K+ is 43–49%, versus typical US tech worker effective rates of 22–24% federal — this compounds the headline comp gap
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate after-tax take-home on both offers, not just gross total comp

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Amazon's historically cash-heavy structure at L5/L6 provides more predictable income but lower upside compared to Google or Meta's equity-heavy structures; personal financial situation affects which mix is preferable
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate your personal financial need for liquid cash income versus tolerance for equity risk; compare the base + bonus cash component across offers before factoring in equity

decision_factors.factor: Graduation year filtering in ATS systems
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Structural hiring infrastructure — not just human bias — filters out 40+ candidates before they reach interviews through graduation year or experience-year count proxies
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate whether your applications are reaching human review or stalling at ATS stage, and whether referral-based applications yield materially better response rates than cold applications

decision_factors.factor: Career stage and level progression runway
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The Canada–US comp gap narrows significantly at senior levels; the absolute gap is largest at mid-career PM roles
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map current level to realistic next 1–2 promotions and model total comp at those levels in both markets

decision_factors.factor: Refresh grant timing and performance rating cycle
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Total comp at a company like Meta or Google compounds significantly if you receive strong performance ratings that trigger above-band refresh grants; a flat performer at the same level receives materially less over time
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask about the refresh grant process, how performance ratings translate to equity refresh, and what the typical range of refresh grants looks like at the target level

decision_factors.factor: Age of hiring manager relative to candidate
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Hiring managers who are 5–10 years younger than a 40+ candidate may experience visible discomfort with authority dynamics — this is a documented pattern in qualitative reports from older job seekers
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research the likely hiring manager's background before interviews; assess whether the interview loop will include people significantly junior to you and prepare to manage those dynamics explicitly

decision_factors.factor: Quality of life and non-financial factors
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The source explicitly frames these as legitimate offsets to the comp gap for Canadian-based PMs
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Treat as a personal weighting factor — the source does not quantify this but presents it as a real variable in the stay-vs-relocate decision

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Silicon Valley and consumer tech hubs have the most pronounced age bias; European-linked companies, government/civic tech, and non-consumer sectors have demonstrably different norms
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research whether target companies have European headquarters, government contracts, or enterprise customer bases that correlate with more age-diverse PM teams

decision_factors.factor: Company funding stage for Canadian scale-ups
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Equity compensation at Canadian fintech and scale-ups varies significantly by funding stage and growth trajectory
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review most recent funding round, revenue trajectory, and IPO likelihood before assigning any value to equity component

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether LMIA is required and which employers will realistically consider you, dramatically affecting the size of the job market you can access
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify exactly: PGWP (open), Canadian PR/citizen (open), employer-specific permit (restricted), expired/no authorization (LMIA or new permit required)

decision_factors.factor: Energy source: problem-solving vs. people development
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The majority of weekly time on each track is spent on the activity that defines it — IC on deep strategy, management on 1:1s and hiring. If the core activity drains you, no amount of comp or title compensates.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Reflect on past weeks: did unblocking a teammate's career problem or conducting a hiring debrief feel rewarding or like overhead? Did solving a hard product problem independently feel more satisfying than coordinating others to solve it?

decision_factors.why_it_matters: If you're already at a company MBA candidates aspire to reach, the MBA's recruiting funnel value is zero or negative
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: is my current employer one that recruits from M7 MBA programs? If yes, the MBA gets you back to where you are.

decision_factors.factor: Career altitude at time of pivot
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Most viable pivot paths (VC, EIR, CoS at meaningful companies) require GPM/Director+ level; pivoting earlier limits destination quality
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether your current title and scope match the minimum bar cited in job descriptions for target pivot roles

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Titles are cosmetic and company-specific; level codes map to actual scope, compensation bands, and promotion timelines that can be compared across companies
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask directly for the numeric or alphanumeric level code and cross-reference against a known leveling map (e.g., the FAANG equivalency table in this source)

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Risk tolerance changes completely based on whether you have a mortgage, dependents, or other fixed obligations — the same startup offer is a rational bet at 25 and a dangerous one at 38 with kids
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Inventory fixed monthly obligations (mortgage/rent, dependents, debt service) and calculate whether base salary alone at the startup covers them without equity

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Learning rate predicts where you'll be in 3–5 years more than current compensation or title; a high learning rate compounds, a low one stagnates
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether you've done something in the last 6 months that surprised you — something you didn't know you could do; if you can't answer, the role isn't growing you

decision_factors.why_it_matters: A single data point is noise; a sustained trend below threshold signals a structural problem that won't self-resolve
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Track a 1-10 satisfaction rating regularly over months and look for directional trends, not just snapshots

decision_factors.factor: Current career stage (execution vs. strategy vs. org leadership)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The definition of 'great' changes entirely at each stage — skills that earned promotion in Stage 1 are insufficient and potentially irrelevant for Stage 2 advancement
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine whether your current role requires you to execute against a defined scope (Stage 1), define the scope and make the case for it (Stage 2), or build and lead a team beyond your individual output (Stage 3)

decision_factors.why_it_matters: The defining difference between PM and Senior PM is not execution quality but whether the person sets the scope versus works within a defined scope — this determines readiness for promotion
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: Am I defining what problems to solve and why, or am I executing against a direction handed to me? Can I point to a vision and strategic framework I authored?

decision_factors.factor: Organizational headroom at the next level
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If there are no open roles or headcount at the next level, performance is irrelevant to promotion timing — the ceiling is structural, not personal
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask your manager directly whether there is a role to promote into; observe whether anyone at the next level has been hired or promoted recently

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Scope — the actual decision authority and surface area of work — is the strongest predictor of long-term career development; without expanding scope, title and compensation gains do not translate into genuine capability growth
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: what decisions am I actually empowered to make? How large is the surface area of product I own? Has this grown in the last 12–18 months?

decision_factors.factor: Nationality relative to TN visa eligibility
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether the Canada → US TN pathway is accessible and on what timeline, which changes the long-term strategic value of pursuing Canadian PR
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Canadian or Mexican citizen = TN available now; non-North American national = TN requires citizenship, adding 3+ years to the path

decision_factors.why_it_matters: IC track (Staff/Principal) roles exist almost exclusively at large tech companies and represent only 10–15% of the PM job market. Management roles are available at every company size and represent 30–40% of PM roles.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether you want or need flexibility to work at startups, mid-size companies, or outside major tech hubs. If yes, IC track significantly constrains your options.

decision_factors.why_it_matters: The further your background is from PM (e.g., investment banking vs. engineering), the more the MBA credential and recruiting funnel does real work
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map your background against direct PM transition difficulty: engineers and designers can transition without MBA; finance professionals face more gatekeeping

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Roles like EIR and founding require demonstrated ability to build new products from scratch; a scaling-only background disqualifies candidates for these paths
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Audit your portfolio: how many products did you create from nothing vs. inherit and grow?

decision_factors.factor: Total compensation vs. market median for that level
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Comp below the median for a stated level signals either a soft downlevel or a company underpaying relative to its own bands — both are red flags
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Look up levels.fyi median total comp for the specific company and level code; flag any offer more than 10–15% below median

decision_factors.why_it_matters: A startup's burn rate and runway determine whether your equity has any time to vest and whether you'll still have a job in 18 months
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask directly for MRR, customer churn rates, current burn rate, runway until next funding round, path to profitability, and contingency plans if funding fails — treat inability to answer specifically as a red flag

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Real ownership — the ability to say no and have your judgment respected — is the core mechanism by which PM skills develop; without it, you build activity habits, not impact habits
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the hiring team to name two recent decisions the PM made independently and what happened when they got something wrong; vague answers mean authority is nominal

decision_factors.factor: What the current environment teaches vs. what you're missing
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Large and small companies develop fundamentally different instincts; your career stage determines which gap is more costly
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Audit your experience: have you had radical ownership? Have you operated at scale with complex stakeholders? Identify which instinct is underdeveloped

decision_factors.factor: Scope of current responsibilities relative to target level
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Operating at the wrong scope — even with technical competence on every listed skill — will block promotion; scope must precede title
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare the areas you are currently defining and owning versus areas assigned to you; assess whether you are identifying opportunities or executing against identified ones

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Senior PMs build trust by proactively communicating decisions and proposals rather than waiting for instructions — managers use this signal to gauge readiness for greater independence
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review your last 5 manager conversations: did you bring proposed approaches, or did you bring problems waiting for answers?

decision_factors.why_it_matters: A champion with low organizational influence cannot move promotion decisions even with genuine advocacy — the quality of the champion matters more than having one
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Observe who speaks in leadership forums, whose recommendations get acted on, and who participates in calibration sessions at your level

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Career growth ultimately rests on you, but your manager can either accelerate your trajectory or cap it; knowing which one you have determines whether staying or leaving is the right move
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Attempt the partnership conversation (ask what gap exists between you and the next level); a manager who engages constructively is an accelerant, one who deflects or gives vague answers is likely a ceiling

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Many Canadian startups and mid-size companies refuse to do LMIA due to cost and time, effectively excluding candidates who require it from a large portion of the market
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine employer category: large tech (Amazon CA, Microsoft CA, major banks) = will do LMIA; startups/mid-size = often will not; assess via job posting language or direct recruiter inquiry

decision_factors.why_it_matters: At VP+ and CPO level, management track has a higher compensation ceiling ($480K–$750K+) compared to IC Distinguished levels ($500K+). The divergence only matters if reaching executive level is a realistic and desired goal.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Honestly assess whether VP or CPO is a realistic target given your trajectory, and whether maximizing total compensation at that level is a primary life goal — not just an aspirational preference.

decision_factors.why_it_matters: For non-US candidates without US work authorization or recruiting networks, MBA provides H-1B sponsorship pathway and campus recruiting access — a structurally different value proposition
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess current visa status, existing US recruiting network access, and whether target employers sponsor H-1B for experienced hires

decision_factors.factor: Existing thought leadership and public presence
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For VC and consulting pivots, public credibility as an opinion-maker accelerates entry; its absence creates a cold-start problem
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether you have published writing, conference talks, or a newsletter that demonstrates domain expertise to strangers

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Real scope is defined by what decisions you can make unilaterally without escalation, not by what the title or org chart implies
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: 'What decisions can I make without approval?' and 'Who has override authority over my roadmap or prioritization?'

decision_factors.factor: Equity structure details (liquidation preferences, exercise window)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Two offers with identical equity percentages can have radically different actual payouts depending on liquidation preference stacking and exercise window length
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask for the cap table summary, liquidation preference terms on all existing rounds, and exercise window length (90 days vs. 5-year extended windows are materially different)

decision_factors.why_it_matters: The blast radius of your decisions, the strategic ambiguity you must resolve, and the stakeholders who depend on your judgment determine how fast you grow toward genuinely senior capability
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare what the most important decision you'll make in the next 12 months is; assess number of stakeholders, ambiguity level, and organizational surface area

decision_factors.why_it_matters: The ability to learn new skills quickly as the job changes matters more than current static competency, because job requirements change
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Reflect on how quickly you've come up to speed in past role changes and whether you've actively sought unfamiliar domains

decision_factors.factor: Visibility of your judgment to decision-makers
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Sound judgment that is not demonstrated explicitly cannot build trust, which is required for expanded autonomy and scope at senior levels
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Audit recent decisions: did you share your reasoning framework, alternatives considered, and rationale — or just the outcome? Do executives know how you think?

decision_factors.factor: Ability to hold and reason through competing valid perspectives
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Senior decisions increasingly have no clean right answer — the capacity to reason through tradeoffs without prematurely resolving ambiguity is a senior-level cognitive requirement
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Observe whether you can articulate the conditions under which different answers would each be correct, without defaulting to a single rigid framework

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Impact that isn't communicated and documented doesn't exist in calibration conversations — the decision is made on available evidence
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask yourself: if your manager had to describe your last 6 months of impact in a calibration meeting, could they do it specifically and compellingly without your help

decision_factors.factor: Joy vs. Ego weighting in a role
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Roles that satisfy ego (sound impressive externally) but lack joy (genuine meaning and energy) accelerate career stagnation, not growth, because sustained high performance requires intrinsic motivation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Honestly separate what makes you look good from what you find energizing; ask whether you would take the role if no one else knew about it

decision_factors.factor: Career ambition horizon: scope vs. stability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Canada offers immigration security and lifestyle advantages; US offers higher comp and larger product scope — the right choice depends on which dimension the candidate is optimizing for
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether the candidate's priority is maximizing PM career portfolio and comp, or securing long-term residency and work-life balance; these favor different geographies at different career stages

decision_factors.factor: Comfort with formal vs. informal authority
decision_factors.why_it_matters: IC PMs must influence without formal authority across their entire career. Management PMs exercise formal authority but also bear direct accountability for other people's performance and career outcomes.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Recall situations where you had to drive outcomes without direct control. Did that feel like a natural challenge or a frustrating structural problem? Frustration signals management fit; comfort signals IC fit.

decision_factors.why_it_matters: The real cost includes 2 years of lost salary and missed promotion cycles — PMs promoted to Staff/Director during your MBA years keep compounding ahead
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate: tuition + living ($247K average for M7) + 2 years of foregone salary + value of missed promotion cycle at your current trajectory

decision_factors.why_it_matters: First consulting clients come from former colleagues; VC roles come through existing VC relationships; without domain network, timelines extend significantly
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count how many current VCs, founders, or operators in your target domain you have a genuine relationship with (not just LinkedIn connections)

decision_factors.why_it_matters: A lower title at a higher-tier company can open more future doors than a higher title at a lower-tier company, making the brand itself a compensating factor
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether hiring managers at your next target companies would respond more favorably to the new company's name on your resume

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Actual scope of ownership determines learning velocity, resume credibility, and career trajectory more than title or compensation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: What will I own? What decisions will I make unilaterally vs. need approval for? Who will I influence organizationally? Compare answers across offers directly

decision_factors.factor: Skill gap vs. org ceiling diagnosis
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The correct response to a skill gap (stay and fix it) is the opposite of the correct response to an org ceiling (leave); misdiagnosis leads to years of misdirected effort
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check if feedback is consistent across multiple managers and reviews (skill gap) vs. politically colored and inconsistent (org signal); check if scope expanded or contracted in the last 6 months

decision_factors.factor: Stage of career progression (feature vs. product vs. business vs. org)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The scale of what you're building defines what skills are actually required; title alone is misleading
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess not your title but the scope of what you own: are you building a feature, a product, a business, or an organization?

decision_factors.why_it_matters: What actually matters to stakeholders often differs from what they say matters; understanding this gap determines whether you can move work through the organization
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify key stakeholders and gatekeepers; assess whether you know their actual priorities, resistance triggers, and what scrappiness is acceptable versus what violates unspoken rules

decision_factors.factor: Alignment of work to long-term vision vs. incremental delivery
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Junior PMs focus on shipping value incrementally; senior PMs connect every decision to a long-term vision — this shift in orientation signals strategic maturity
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: Can I draw a direct line from today's work to a 2–3 year vision? Do I have a documented strategic framework that explains why this bet over alternatives?

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Promotion requires demonstrated performance at the next level — scope is the prerequisite for that demonstration
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare the cross-functional reach, business stakes, and strategic visibility of your current work against what people at the next level typically own

decision_factors.factor: Visibility of your work to decision-makers
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Promotion decisions are made by committees with presentation bias; if the people who decide your level cannot see your impact, your actual performance is partially irrelevant
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: do the people in my promotion calibration know what I have done and why it mattered? Would they cite my work unprompted?

decision_factors.factor: Whether an intra-company transfer pathway exists
decision_factors.why_it_matters: ICT is LMIA-exempt and fast; if a candidate's current employer has Canadian operations, this is significantly easier than any external hiring pathway
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether current employer (especially US-based tech) has a Canadian entity; if yes, ICT C-12 exemption is likely available

decision_factors.why_it_matters: The IC → Management transition is achievable in your 30s–40s. The Management → IC transition after years of management experience is significantly harder and often means accepting lower scope.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess how risk-averse you are about foreclosing future options. If optionality matters greatly, IC first preserves more paths. If you are confident in management fit now, the cost of delay is also real.

decision_factors.why_it_matters: CPO-track technical PM roles do not commonly require or benefit from MBA; GM, COO, and strategy-adjacent leadership roles do
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify the 5 job postings for your 5-year target role and check what credentials/backgrounds those people hold

decision_factors.factor: Tolerance for delayed and uncertain feedback loops
decision_factors.why_it_matters: VC outcomes take years vs. weeks for product metrics; founders operate without the validation loops PMs are trained on
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Reflect on whether you have sustained motivation and judgment confidence in environments where outcome signals are slow or absent

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Accepting a downlevel only makes sense if there is a clear, stated path and realistic timeline back to your target level
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: 'What are the stated promotion criteria from this level to the next, and what is the typical time-to-promo for high performers?'

decision_factors.factor: Career stage and desired trajectory (5-year vision)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The right choice depends entirely on where you want to be in 5 years — specific skills needed, network required, and financial position targeted
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Define the 5-year target with specificity (not 'senior leader' but specific skills, network type, and financial position), then evaluate which path creates more of those prerequisites

decision_factors.factor: Manager's ability and willingness to advocate
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A manager who is political, checked out, or below the influence threshold cannot advocate for you even if they want to; your promotion depends heavily on their organizational capital
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether your manager understands what you want to do next, can describe a path to it, and has the political standing to fight for you in headcount and promotion discussions

decision_factors.factor: Quality of your personal board of directors
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Without diverse, honest feedback, you're navigating your career with a biased map
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether you have mentors ahead of you, peers at your level, mentors from outside product, and people who will tell you hard truths — not just encouragers

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Leaders who are viewed as defensive or self-interested will not be given expanded scope regardless of execution quality; leaders actively want to work with certain PMs and merely tolerate others
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Collect 360-degree feedback specifically on whether peers describe you as constructive, humble, and collaborative in escalations and disagreements

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Senior PMs do not prioritize their own team's goals over the organization's — failure to internalize this leads to decisions that optimize locally but damage broader trust and outcomes
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether your recent decisions accounted for constraints and goals of adjacent teams, or whether they were optimized purely for your own team's metrics

decision_factors.factor: Specificity and visibility of gap-closure progress
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Vague feedback loops allow promotion to be deferred indefinitely; named, tracked gaps with agreed definitions of 'fixed' create accountability
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether you and your manager have co-defined exactly what 'closing the gap' looks like and are reviewing progress on a regular cadence

decision_factors.factor: Peer network and coaching circle quality
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Peer groups provide pattern recognition across organizations that helps you distinguish industry norms from company-specific dysfunction — a critical diagnostic for career decisions
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Do you have at least a small group of peers at similar career stages outside your company with whom you discuss real decisions? Do those relationships predate any urgent need?

decision_factors.factor: Global Talent Stream eligibility for the specific PM role
decision_factors.why_it_matters: GTS reduces LMIA processing from 2–5 months to 2 weeks, making it viable where standard LMIA is not; eligibility depends on NOC code of the PM role
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Verify whether the PM role is classified under NOC 20012; if so, employer may qualify for GTS expedited processing

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Both tracks carry significant stress, but of different types. IC stress is political influence and being right with no formal authority. Management stress is direct people accountability — performance management, firing, career conversations.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Consider which stress type you have more coping capacity for. Neither is objectively harder, but individuals vary significantly in which type they can sustain over a decade.

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Non-target undergrad + non-FAANG early career creates a credential stack that closes specific recruiting doors; M7 MBA can reset this
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Test directly: apply to target roles and measure response rates — if doors are closed, identify whether MBA is the specific key or if other factors are blocking

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Consulting takes 12–18 months to replace income; founding involves unpaid or underpaid periods; CoS roles may involve pay cuts
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate how many months of living expenses you have saved and what minimum income you need during a transition period

decision_factors.factor: Scope size relative to current role
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A lower title with materially larger scope is a real promotion; a higher title with smaller scope is a real demotion regardless of what the offer letter says
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare team size, product complexity, cross-functional reach, and autonomy between current and target roles

decision_factors.factor: Manager quality and team shipping record
decision_factors.why_it_matters: At Big Tech, manager quality and recent team output predict your actual learning and promotion trajectory more than org brand
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask what the team shipped in the last 12 months (ask for 3 specific products), how the manager makes decisions, promotion time-to-promo at your level in this specific org, and why the role exists

decision_factors.factor: Company trajectory alignment with industry direction
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Staying at a company moving against industry direction limits your external market value and narrows the problems you'll encounter
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate whether the company's bets are in domains growing in importance; assess whether your external network credibility is growing or stagnating

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Mentors advise you directly; sponsors advocate for you in rooms you're not in — you need both for advancement
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify whether anyone in your network actively advocates for you in promotion or opportunity discussions without you present

decision_factors.factor: Ability to articulate an inspiring vision
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A senior PM who cannot articulate why their area matters at the company level will be deprioritized in resource allocation conversations
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Test whether you can explain your product area's connection to company strategy in a way that energizes listeners — not just informs them

decision_factors.factor: Time in role at Senior IC level before pursuing management
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The typical path requires 1–2 years at Senior IC before moving to Manager of PMs — moving too early risks skipping the consolidation needed to lead other PMs effectively
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess how long you have held the Senior IC title and whether you have demonstrated the three differentiators (strategy, autonomy, nuance) consistently across that period

decision_factors.factor: Number of promotion cycles already passed
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Multiple cycles with the same feedback is a signal that the block is systemic or political, not developmental
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count how many review cycles have passed with positive reviews but no promotion; assess whether the feedback has materially changed or remains identical

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Because presentations disproportionately determine how you are judged, a gap in communication skills relative to peers compounds negatively over time in promotion and influence outcomes
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Seek explicit feedback on high-visibility presentations; observe whether you are included or excluded from high-stakes communication opportunities

decision_factors.factor: Time already accrued in TEER 1 Canadian work experience
decision_factors.why_it_matters: 12 months of TEER 1 experience is the threshold for CEC eligibility; every month matters when calculating how close the candidate is to PR eligibility
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count continuous months in NOC TEER 0 or 1 role on valid Canadian work authorization; assess gap to 12-month threshold

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Technical product roles (B2B, developer tools, infrastructure) value domain depth over MBA credentials; MBA may signal the wrong direction
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess the product type of your target roles and whether hiring managers in that space value or discount MBA credentials

decision_factors.factor: Specific market thesis or domain expertise
decision_factors.why_it_matters: PM-to-founder requires a specific, defensible thesis about a market gap; generalist product experience alone is insufficient to credibly found a company
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Can you articulate a precise, non-obvious insight about a market that your product experience uniquely positions you to act on?

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Startup titles often come with equity as the intended compensation premium, but equity value is highly uncertain and should not be treated as equivalent to cash or vested RSUs
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Model equity at 0%, 1x, and 5x outcomes; only count equity as a compensating factor if the base + cash comp alone is acceptable

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Startup success opens all doors; startup failure opens startup doors but not Big Tech; Big Tech opens most doors but can pigeonhole — sequencing affects which doors stay open
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map the likely resume outcomes (success, failure, middling) for each path and assess which downstream options matter most to you

decision_factors.factor: Career stage fit with company stage
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Early-career PMs benefit from structure and craft-building at larger companies; mid-career PMs need ambiguity and high-stakes ownership that large structured environments can no longer provide
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify whether you need to build craft (favor process-heavy environments) or judgment under ambiguity (favor earlier-stage, higher-ownership environments)

decision_factors.why_it_matters: At senior levels, PMs are expected to help grow the team; inability to write job descriptions, pitch candidates, or conduct effective interviews caps team growth and signals limited senior readiness
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether you have been involved in hiring, whether you can write a compelling job description, and whether you can close candidates on your team's vision

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Structural constraints like tenure requirements or frozen budgets make promotion impossible regardless of performance, and misreading them as performance feedback is costly
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask HR or your manager directly about minimum tenure per level and whether the upcoming cycle has budget for promotions

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Higher pre-MBA salary means higher opportunity cost — a $150K finance professional has different break-even math than a $250K Senior PM
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Run the specific break-even calculation: does MBA-enabled comp trajectory exceed current trajectory by more than total opportunity cost over remaining career?

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Failing at founding at 40+ while trying to return to a large-company PM role creates documented friction; the cost of a failed pivot compounds with age
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Model the re-entry scenario explicitly: if the pivot fails in 3 years, what does your PM job search look like at that age?

decision_factors.why_it_matters: An inflated title from a lower-tier company can make a PM look overleveled to hiring managers at target companies, reducing hiring appeal for roles that would actually be the right fit
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether future target company hiring managers would view the current title as appropriately scoped or suspiciously senior

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Startup provides breadth and speed under uncertainty; Big Tech provides depth and formal training — the right choice depends on which gap you need to fill
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Audit your current skill gaps: if you lack breadth and exposure to ambiguity, startup accelerates; if you lack structured frameworks and scale exposure, Big Tech accelerates

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Switching companies to escape feedback or avoid hard situations doesn't remove the underlying skill gap — it relocates it to a new context without the institutional knowledge you had before
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask honestly whether the reasons for leaving are organizational (no path, no scope, political block) or personal (hard feedback, discomfort, conflict); if personal, address before leaving

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Avoiding surprises is a trust-building mechanism — executives who are caught off guard lose confidence in PMs regardless of outcomes
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Audit whether you proactively share the right information up and down the chain, and whether you flag problems early rather than surfacing them at crisis point

decision_factors.factor: External market value at next-level title
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The market frequently offers the next-level title faster than your current employer — knowing this changes the cost-benefit of staying vs. leaving
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Run a parallel job search or engage recruiters to benchmark what title and comp the market would offer you today

decision_factors.why_it_matters: MBA→PM placement rates dropped sharply post-2022; the same credential investment in a down hiring market produces worse outcomes
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research current-year placement data from target schools, not historical averages; check whether target companies are actively running MBA PM recruiting programs

decision_factors.why_it_matters: VC is an influence-only relationship with portfolio companies; PMs accustomed to owning decisions must genuinely adapt to an advisory posture
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess how comfortable you are with outcomes being determined by founders you advise rather than decisions you make directly

decision_factors.factor: MBA as filter in target domain
decision_factors.why_it_matters: MBA is a genuine filter in some domains (consulting, PE-backed product, certain enterprise environments) and largely irrelevant in others (tech PM promotion to Director)
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify whether the specific role or domain you're targeting uses MBA as a real hiring or promotion filter, not just a preference signal

decision_factors.factor: Interest in learning from a specific leader vs. independent operation
decision_factors.why_it_matters: CoS is the right path when the primary motivation is altitude exposure and mentorship from a specific executive; it is the wrong path if the goal is autonomous ownership
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify whether you have a specific leader whose decision-making you want to learn from; if not, CoS may not be the right vehicle

decision_factors.factor: Work authorization clarity in job search materials
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Canadian employers often misread 'work permit' as requiring sponsorship, filtering candidates out before qualifications are reviewed
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether your resume and cover letter explicitly state: open work permit, no employer action required, PR being pursued independently

decision_factors.why_it_matters: A 1-year PGWP from a post-grad certificate gives you far less runway to accumulate the 1 year of Canadian experience required for CEC eligibility, find a job, and begin Express Entry — any job search delay can consume a disproportionate share of permit time
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check program length: PGWP = length of program, capped at 3 years. A 2-year master's yields a 3-year PGWP; a 1-year program yields only 1 year

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Whether a company routinely sponsors H-1B visas determines whether your future status is viable there — large tech companies have established processes; small startups often don't
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask explicitly during late-stage interviews; check LinkedIn for international employees at the company; look at H-1B disclosure data (LCA filings are public)

decision_factors.factor: Who you target in the org (manager vs. HR vs. recruiter)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether you enter a screening conversation or a problem-solving conversation; managers can create roles or advocate; HR can only filter against existing criteria
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Use LinkedIn to identify the likely direct hiring manager for the team you want to join; look for eng leads, product leads, or team leads — not talent acquisition titles

decision_factors.factor: Advisor's industry network and internship pipeline
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Directly determines whether a PhD student gets internships and return offers at top industry research labs, often more than program prestige does
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the advisor directly where their last 5 students interned and where they ended up; cross-check on LinkedIn

decision_factors.why_it_matters: The number of months left on STEM OPT directly constrains which options are viable — finding a new sponsor, pursuing a bridge employer, or switching status all have different lead times
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate months remaining and map against the next H-1B cap registration window; if fewer than ~6 months remain before registration opens, urgency escalates sharply

decision_factors.factor: Team culture revealed during interview process
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A team that treats interviews as purely technical screenings likely doesn't invest in people; this predicts your experience post-join
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask substantive questions about product vision and team composition; observe whether the interviewer engages with you as a person or only tests skills

decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: Do I have N years in a single industry vertical with genuine insight into its sub-segments, or am I spread across industries? If the former, strategic PM path is viable; if the latter, hybrid expansion is the realistic next move

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Referral response rates (~30%) dramatically outperform cold applications (~2%), and the Canadian job market appears particularly network-dependent
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count how many Canada-based contacts you have who can actively refer you vs. how many you are cold-applying through

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Canadian employers heavily value co-op experience as a proxy for 'Canadian experience' — having it significantly reduces hiring friction
decision_factors.how_to_assess: If you completed a co-op during your Canadian program, make it prominent on your resume and LinkedIn; if you did not, expect to address the 'Canadian experience' gap explicitly

decision_factors.factor: Current visa stage (OPT vs. STEM OPT vs. H-1B needed)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Each stage carries a different ask on the employer — OPT requires nothing, STEM OPT requires E-Verify enrollment and I-983 filing, H-1B requires attorney fees and lottery risk
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Know your own timeline: when does your OPT expire, are you STEM-eligible, when would H-1B cap registration apply

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Too few follow-ups leaves responses on the table; too many signals desperation and damages the relationship; the right cadence maximizes response rate without cost
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Use the day 4 / day 9 rule; track touches per contact; move to a different person after three unanswered touches

decision_factors.factor: Target role type: academic researcher vs. industry researcher vs. applied scientist vs. SWE
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Each destination has different PhD requirements, different program selection criteria, and different ROI calculations; conflating them leads to suboptimal program or advisor choices
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map your target role to its actual requirements: faculty needs top-5 program + publications; Research Scientist at DeepMind needs strong publications; Applied Scientist at Amazon needs applied relevance + internships; SWE needs no PhD

decision_factors.factor: Existence of written vs. verbal sponsorship commitment
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether the employee has any legal recourse or leverage; verbal promises provide almost none
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review offer letter, email, Slack, or any written communication where sponsorship was mentioned; written evidence strengthens a potential promissory estoppel claim

decision_factors.factor: Whether the new role offers love for the product and a sense of mission
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The best-answer author (a PM) argues that without these two emotional connections, the work will be unsustainable regardless of compensation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask yourself: do I use this product daily? Do I believe in what this team is building? If neither, flag it

decision_factors.factor: Scope of ownership at each career level (feature → product line → domain → department → company)

decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify what scope you currently own (single feature module, full product line, domain-level cross-functional work, or department-level P&L/strategy) and what the next scope level requires

decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: can people in adjacent teams or functions articulate what you've built and its impact? If not, you have a visibility gap
