failure_patterns.pattern: Spending the first 4–6 weeks only cold-applying with no networking activity
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Job board applications feel productive and scalable; networking feels uncertain and slow — but the ROI is inverted in the Canadian tech market
failure_patterns.consequence: Weeks of low response rates before discovering that referrals produce 15x higher response rates; wasted runway on PGWP timeline
warning_signs: Submitting 20+ applications per week with under 5% response rate
Not attending any local tech events or meetups in first month of search

failure_patterns.pattern: Failing to verify that your Canadian work experience qualifies under NOC TEER 0–3 before relying on it for CEC eligibility
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates assume that any white-collar or professional job automatically qualifies — the TEER classification system is not intuitive and many job titles map ambiguously
failure_patterns.consequence: Reaching the 1-year mark and discovering the experience is not CEC-qualifying, losing months of immigration runway
warning_signs: Candidate has never looked up their NOC code
Candidate assumes their job title is self-evidently TEER 1 without checking

failure_patterns.pattern: Conflating OPT authorization with employer sponsorship when answering 'are you authorized to work?'
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates confuse their own visa status with the employer's action — OPT is granted by USCIS to the student, but it feels like something the employer is responsible for
failure_patterns.consequence: Candidate answers 'no' or hedges when the correct answer is 'yes,' causing unnecessary early-stage rejection or recruiter confusion
warning_signs: Saying 'I'm on a student visa so I'd need sponsorship' when asked about current work authorization
Treating OPT and H-1B as the same category of ask

failure_patterns.pattern: Emailing HR directly as the cold outreach target
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: HR contacts are more publicly visible and feel 'safer' to approach; HR titles signal hiring-related work so feel like the logical target
failure_patterns.consequence: HR roles include screening for sponsorship eligibility as a primary filter; cold emails to HR are routed into the same rejection funnel as portal applications
warning_signs: Cold emails sent to talent acquisition, recruiter, or HR business partner titles
Emails that open with role availability or job application framing

failure_patterns.pattern: Pursuing a PhD without a research-specific career goal, defaulting to SWE afterward
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: PhD feels like a safe, prestigious credential; students underestimate the opportunity cost and overestimate the credential's transferability to non-research roles
failure_patterns.consequence: 4-5 years of foregone high SWE income with no meaningful salary premium upon exit; peers who entered industry directly have more experience and higher total earnings
warning_signs: Cannot articulate a specific research goal or publication target
Primary stated reason for PhD is 'it seems like a good credential' or 'I like learning'
Has not investigated whether target SWE roles require or reward a PhD

failure_patterns.pattern: Assuming alternative visa pathways (L-1, O-1) are viable fallbacks without checking eligibility criteria
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: These statuses are mentioned in immigration discussions as options, so people assume they are accessible; the high bars for each are not commonly understood
failure_patterns.consequence: Time is wasted investigating paths that are not available, compressing the window to find realistic solutions
warning_signs: No prior employment at a qualifying multinational abroad (eliminates L-1)
No documented record of extraordinary achievement in the field (eliminates O-1)

failure_patterns.pattern: Herd-following job switches during 'golden hiring season'
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Social contagion — seeing colleagues interview creates FOMO and normalizes switching even without personal readiness
failure_patterns.consequence: Switches made without self-assessment land in roles that don't advance your career; you arrive at a new company without clear goals
warning_signs: You started thinking about switching after a colleague announced their departure
You cannot articulate what specifically you want from the new role
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_互联网人跳槽的注意事项有哪些.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Treating career path as a linear ladder (PM → Senior PM → Director → VP → CEO) rather than a branching decision tree
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: The linear ladder model is the most commonly cited framework in Chinese PM communities and feels logical — it mirrors corporate org charts — so people optimize for title progression rather than capability architecture
failure_patterns.consequence: PMs pursue promotion within a single track without recognizing that the skills required diverge significantly at each fork, leading to mismatched role expectations and underperformance at the next level
warning_signs: PM frames career goal as 'I want to become a product director in 2 years' without specifying what type of director or what domain
PM treats scope expansion as automatic with tenure rather than as something requiring deliberate demonstration
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_产品经理工作_3_5_年后有哪些发展路径.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Staying in the 0-1 mindset (skill-building mode) past year 3–5
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Foundational skill development feels safe and measurable; committing to a specific business domain feels constraining and risky
failure_patterns.consequence: PM remains a generalist executor while peers who went deep in a domain pull ahead in compensation and title — becomes harder to course-correct as years pass
warning_signs: Still describing career goals primarily in terms of tools or methodologies at year 4+
Resisting domain specialization because 'I want to keep my options open'
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_产品经理应该如何进行职业规划.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Assuming that getting older means losing relevance (treating PM as a youth job)
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Cultural association of 'innovation' with youth; early internet culture rewarded novelty over depth, creating a belief that older PMs are less valuable
failure_patterns.consequence: PMs preemptively downgrade their ambitions or exit the field when they still have compounding advantages in domain knowledge and business judgment
warning_signs: Expressing anxiety about age relative to peers
Framing career questions around 'how much longer can I do this' rather than 'what am I building toward'
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_产品经理的职业生涯规划是怎么样的.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Presenting B2B work without quantified commercial outcomes
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: B2B PMs often work on long-cycle products where revenue data is delayed or attributed to multiple teams; they present process work instead
failure_patterns.consequence: Evaluators cannot assess business impact; the promotion case is weak even if the work was genuinely strong
warning_signs: Your outcomes section describes features shipped rather than revenue or client acquisition impact
You don't know the win rate or conversion data for the products you own
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_产品经理要如何晋升_有哪些晋升路径.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Staying in execution mode past the 5-year mark without building influence or business ownership
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Execution is comfortable, measurable, and safe; influence-building is ambiguous and politically risky; PMs default to doing more of what they're already good at
failure_patterns.consequence: At 35+, they are competing directly with lower-cost junior PMs on execution tasks and cannot justify their seniority premium
warning_signs: Your most recent performance review is defined entirely by feature delivery metrics
You have not mentored or grown any junior PMs in the past year
Your work product could be replicated by someone with 2-3 years less experience
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_那些35岁以上的产品经理都去做什么了.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Not raising sponsorship needs until after receiving an offer
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Fear of rejection at any earlier stage causes candidates to delay disclosure, rationalizing that getting the offer first improves leverage
failure_patterns.consequence: Offer is rescinded or acceptance is delayed while company scrambles to assess feasibility — damages relationship and wastes pipeline time on both sides
warning_signs: Telling oneself 'I'll bring it up if I get an offer'
Completing a full interview loop without once mentioning future sponsorship needs

failure_patterns.pattern: Asking for a job or interview in the first cold email
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: The actual goal is a job, so asking for it directly feels efficient and honest; reduces the perceived 'manipulation' of a multi-step ask
failure_patterns.consequence: High-commitment asks in cold outreach trigger immediate rejection; the recipient has no relationship investment and no reason to take on the work of evaluating a stranger's application
warning_signs: First email contains phrases like 'I'd love to apply for' or 'are you hiring'
Email includes a resume attachment in the first message

failure_patterns.pattern: Overestimating personal market value when detached from a well-known company
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Attribution error — confusing company brand for personal capability; the 'halo effect' of a large employer inflates perceived individual worth
failure_patterns.consequence: Shock when the market doesn't respond to your candidacy as expected; offers come in lower than anticipated
warning_signs: Your confidence in switching is primarily based on your current company's reputation
You haven't independently validated your skills against job postings in the last year
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_互联网人跳槽的注意事项有哪些.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Treating promotion criteria from direct managers as the actual promotion criteria
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Managers at large companies cite official level rubrics (P6, P7, P8) but often don't fully understand what actually drives promotion decisions — structural visibility and political capital matter as much as documented criteria
failure_patterns.consequence: PM meets all stated criteria and is still passed over, feeling blindsided and demoralized
warning_signs: PM can recite the level rubric precisely but has not mapped their internal visibility across teams
PM's promotion strategy is purely about deliverables, not about who knows their name
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_产品经理应该如何进行职业规划.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Type C PM (lower confidence) jumping to a startup at the 2–3 year threshold following peer pressure or market hype
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Social proof — seeing peers jump to startups and succeed (survivorship bias); FOMO about missing a growth window
failure_patterns.consequence: Startup chaos without strong foundational skills leads to overwhelm, poor output quality, and potentially a setback in professional credibility
warning_signs: Justifying the jump with 'everyone else is doing it'
Cannot articulate specific skills they'll develop at the startup vs. staying
Driven by salary or title rather than scope
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_产品经理的职业生涯规划是怎么样的.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Neglecting the 'why you specifically' question in promotion materials
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: PMs focus on proving their team succeeded, not on isolating their individual contribution — especially in collaborative environments where credit is shared
failure_patterns.consequence: Evaluators question whether the results would have happened without this candidate; promotion is deferred pending clearer individual contribution evidence
warning_signs: You describe project outcomes using 'we' throughout with no 'I' moments
You cannot name a specific decision point where your judgment was decisive
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_产品经理要如何晋升_有哪些晋升路径.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Female PMs underinvesting in 'political' skills (撕逼扯皮能力 — resource negotiation, organizational maneuvering) because they find them distasteful
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: The skills required at senior PM levels shift from product craft to organizational politics; many PMs — disproportionately women per the case data — are promoted for craft but underprepared for the political demands of leadership
failure_patterns.consequence: Reaches a leadership position but is perceived as 'not capable enough' by bosses; gets replaced and experiences a cascading downgrade across subsequent roles
warning_signs: You describe your job as 'just doing good product work' without mentioning stakeholder management
You avoid cross-functional conflicts rather than resolving them
Your boss has given feedback about 'leadership presence' or 'influence' rather than product skills
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_那些35岁以上的产品经理都去做什么了.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Writing cold emails over 150 words
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: More context feels more credible; writers want to pre-answer objections; insecurity drives over-explanation
failure_patterns.consequence: Long emails get skimmed or abandoned before the ask; the signal-to-noise ratio drops and the email reads as low-effort form mail
warning_signs: Email includes full resume narrative
Email has more than two paragraphs
Email tries to explain visa situation, project details, and motivation all at once

failure_patterns.pattern: Failing to surface team expectations in the first weeks of a new role
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: New hires feel pressure to demonstrate competence by doing, not asking; onboarding urgency suppresses curiosity about alignment
failure_patterns.consequence: Best-answer author left a promising opportunity after half a month because misalignment was discovered too late; in mature teams there is little recovery room
warning_signs: You have not explicitly discussed what your manager expects you to deliver in the first 30/60/90 days
You are defaulting to your previous company's ways of working without validating fit
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_互联网人跳槽的注意事项有哪些.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: 80%+ of PMs fail to hit stage-appropriate milestones but continue without diagnosing why
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: The standard career narrative focuses on the successful minority; PMs in the majority assume they're on track because they're employed, not because they've hit real milestones
failure_patterns.consequence: Persistent gap between expected and actual seniority; career stagnation that isn't recognized until 5+ years in when opportunities narrow
warning_signs: No clear successful product in portfolio after 3 years
Never been the named owner of a business line
Cannot articulate a structured career retrospective when asked
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_产品经理的职业生涯规划是怎么样的.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Attempting simultaneous cross-specialty and cross-industry career moves
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: PMs overestimate transferability of general product skills and underestimate domain-specific know-how in both the new specialty and new industry
failure_patterns.consequence: Loss of anchoring advantage; difficulty demonstrating expertise in interviews; slower ramp time and credibility deficit in new role
warning_signs: You are targeting roles that require both a different product type (e.g., data product vs. user product) AND a different industry (e.g., fintech vs. edtech)
You cannot point to a single transferable deep skill that applies to the target role
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_产品经理要如何晋升_有哪些晋升路径.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Treating early-career task diversity as a goal rather than a means
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Junior PMs see rotational exposure as building breadth; they mistake variety for learning without recognizing that depth in one domain is what generates promotable expertise
failure_patterns.consequence: 5-6 years in, they have broad but shallow experience and cannot credibly claim domain expertise in any area
warning_signs: You have worked in 3+ different product domains in under 5 years
You describe your experience as 'versatile' but struggle to articulate a specific domain thesis
You are applying for senior roles but cannot point to a product you owned end-to-end for 2+ years
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_那些35岁以上的产品经理都去做什么了.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Management-track PMs abandoning product depth after promotion
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: New managers believe their role is now purely people and process; they stop reviewing product details to signal they trust their team
failure_patterns.consequence: They lose the product credibility that justified their authority; their teams lose alignment; they become organizationally dependent rather than capability-driven leaders
warning_signs: You haven't reviewed a product spec or user flow in the past month
You rely entirely on direct reports to form product opinions before meetings
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_产品经理要如何晋升_有哪些晋升路径.txt

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the PM role at a tech company being filed under SOC 11-3021 (Computer and Information Systems Managers)?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the correct occupational classification is being used for prevailing wage determination and H-1B petition purposes
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Confirm offered wage meets DOL prevailing wage threshold for SOC 11-3021 in the specific metro area
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Evaluate whether SOC 11-1021 or SOC 11-2021 is more appropriate based on actual job duties; misclassification creates LCA and petition risk

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the offered base salary meet or exceed the DOL prevailing wage Level I threshold for SOC 11-3021 in the employment metro area?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Minimum LCA compliance for H-1B filing
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Determine which wage level (I–IV) applies and how many lottery entries result under the wage-weighted system effective February 2026
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Petition cannot be filed without adjusting the offered wage to at least Level I prevailing wage for the location

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the PM candidate have 3–5 years of experience in subordinate roles prior to the management appointment?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate meets the BLS OOH-stated standard experience requirement for SOC 11-3021 roles, relevant to specialty occupation qualification
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Candidate meets standard experience threshold; document subordinate-role experience in petition
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Candidate may not meet typical qualifications for SOC 11-3021; consider whether role should be classified differently or whether exceptional education compensates

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the PM candidate hold a bachelor's degree in CS, IT, or a related field?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate meets the BLS OOH-stated educational standard for Computer and Information Systems Managers, relevant to H-1B specialty occupation determination
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Educational requirement satisfied; note MBA is increasingly common for senior PM roles per BLS
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: May need to establish equivalent education or experience; specialty occupation determination may face challenge

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the employment location in a high-cost tech hub (SF, Seattle, NYC) or a lower-cost market (Austin, rural/non-metro)?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Which prevailing wage schedule applies; determines LCA wage floor and wage level classification
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Apply metro-specific DOL prevailing wage thresholds (e.g., SF SOC 11-3021 Level I ~$170,000)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Apply lower prevailing wage thresholds (e.g., Austin Level I ~$130,000; rural/non-metro often $90,000–$130,000 base salary range)

diagnostic_questions.question: Under the wage-weighted H-1B lottery (effective February 2026), at which DOL wage level is the PM petition being filed?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Number of lottery entries the petition receives: Level I = 1 entry, Level IV = 4 entries
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If Level III or IV: petition receives 3–4 lottery entries, significantly improving selection odds
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If Level I or II: petition receives 1–2 entries; consider whether wage can be increased to reach higher level

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the internal level code for this offer, not just the title?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the title reflects the actual seniority band the company uses internally for compensation and promotion purposes
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Cross-reference the level code against levels.fyi median total comp for that specific code at that company — does the offer match?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Treat the lack of a clear level code as a red flag and push the recruiter to specify it before proceeding with compensation discussion

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your current age, and how many years until you cross the 35 and 40 thresholds?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Where you sit in the documented bias window and how much time you have to build optionality, network, and credentials before structural market friction increases
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If under 35: Are you treating this window as a finite resource and actively building the network and pivots you'll want access to at 40?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If already past 40: Have you adjusted your sector targeting, search timeline, and channel strategy to account for documented market friction, or are you using tactics calibrated to an earlier career stage?

diagnostic_questions.question: Is immigration status or Canadian PR a primary goal, or is this purely a career and compensation decision?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the comp reduction of a Canadian role is acceptable as the price of a non-financial goal or whether it needs to be justified on career/financial terms alone
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Model the comp reduction explicitly as the cost of PR — is it within an acceptable range given the timeline to PR status?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: The decision should be evaluated purely on total comp in USD terms and career scope — apply the lateral vs. senior-role filter

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the year-by-year vesting schedule, and are there annual refresh grants?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Your actual realized income in years 1 through 4, which may be dramatically different from the headline total comp figure
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Model the cash flow scenario with and without stock price appreciation to understand the range of outcomes you are actually accepting
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If there are no refresh grants, the total comp degrades significantly in years 3 and 4 after the initial grant vests — this changes the long-term value of the offer substantially

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you targeting consumer tech IC roles, enterprise/regulated industry roles, or management track roles?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether your search is landing in the highest-bias zone (consumer tech IC) or the lower-bias zones (enterprise, regulated industries, management track) — the same candidate faces dramatically different markets depending on this targeting
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If consumer tech IC: Do you have the specific domain expertise that would make you the obvious hire despite age, or are you competing on general PM skills?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If enterprise or management track: Are you positioning your experience as domain depth and organizational leadership, or defaulting to IC-style positioning that may not resonate with those hiring committees?

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the Canadian employer a US-parented public company, a Canadian public company, or a Canadian private company?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: How to value the equity component of the offer — liquid RSUs vs. illiquid startup equity vs. no equity
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If US-parented public: include RSU value in total comp at current market price; model vesting schedule carefully (especially for Amazon)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If Canadian private: assign near-zero value to equity for financial planning purposes; evaluate the role on base and bonus only

diagnostic_questions.question: How does this offer compare to the levels.fyi median filtered by company, level code, AND metro area?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the offer is below-band, at-band, or above-band for your specific situation — the unfiltered median is not a useful benchmark
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If the offer is at or above median, determine whether there is still room to negotiate equity and signing bonus upward before accepting
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If the offer is below median after filtering, determine whether this reflects a negotiation gap (addressable) or a structural comp culture issue at the company (less addressable)

diagnostic_questions.question: Are your applications reaching human review, or are they stalling at ATS screening?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the friction you are experiencing is structural filtering (graduation year, experience year count) versus human bias — the solutions are different for each
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If applications are reaching humans but not converting: Is the friction concentrated in culture-fit feedback, which may indicate human-level age bias in interview loops?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If applications are not reaching humans: Are you using referral-based applications as your primary channel, or relying on cold applications that expose you to ATS filters disproportionately?

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you converted both offers to USD and compared after-tax take-home, not just gross total comp?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate is aware of the full magnitude of the Canada–US gap including the tax differential
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What is the USD after-tax delta, and what non-financial factors are you treating as offsets to that delta?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Do this calculation before proceeding — the gap is typically 40–50% larger than it appears when comparing gross numbers in local currencies

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the signing bonus, and does it cover your unvested equity at your current company?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the financial switch is net positive or net negative in year one after accounting for equity you are leaving on the table
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If signing bonus exceeds unvested equity, the switch is financially safe in year one — evaluate the multi-year comp trajectory next
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If signing bonus does not cover unvested equity, calculate the break-even point and determine whether the long-term comp upside justifies the short-term loss

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have domain expertise in a regulated or technically specialized industry that a target company could not easily replicate with a younger candidate?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you have the primary counter to age bias available to 40+ PMs — domain depth that creates a specific, hard-to-replace value proposition
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If yes: Are you targeting companies where that domain expertise is a hiring requirement, or applying broadly and competing on general PM skills?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If no: What is your timeline for building that domain depth, and is your current role giving you the domain exposure needed to create that differentiation before 40?

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the Canadian role a title and scope increase relative to your current role, or a lateral move?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether there is career upside to offset the comp reduction
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: How many years would it take to reach that level organically at your current employer, and what is the comp difference over that period?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: A lateral move to Canada with a comp cut has no career justification — the only justification is immigration or quality of life

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the role at a FAANG or equivalent major tech company, or a non-FAANG large tech company?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you should benchmark against FAANG comp tables or non-FAANG benchmarks, since conflating them leads to systematic misvaluation in either direction
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Use company-specific levels.fyi data for Google, Meta, Amazon, or LinkedIn rather than aggregate PM salary data
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Compare against Intuit-equivalent benchmarks; note that Principal PM at strong non-FAANG can match FAANG Senior PM total comp, so do not automatically assume FAANG is superior

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the age distribution of the PM team at your target companies, and what is the age of the likely hiring manager?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: The actual cultural context you are walking into — a hiring manager 10 years younger than you, interviewing you for a peer-level role, is a documented friction point that requires active management
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If the team is age-diverse: Is that diversity concentrated in management roles or also present at the IC level you are targeting?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If the team is uniformly young: Is this a consumer tech company where age bias is structurally embedded, and have you considered whether targeting this company is worth the friction relative to enterprise or management track alternatives?

diagnostic_questions.question: For Amazon Canada offers: have you modeled Year 1 cash flow specifically, not just the 4-year average?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate understands Amazon's uneven RSU vesting and can sustain their financial obligations in Year 1
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Is Year 1 take-home sufficient for your fixed costs in the new location including Toronto or Vancouver housing costs?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Request the RSU vesting schedule breakdown by year before accepting — Year 1 is the lowest and may be significantly below the headline number

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you received 'overqualified' feedback, and if so, how are you interpreting it?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the PM is internalizing structural market friction as personal performance feedback — 'overqualified' is a documented proxy for age-related cost and tenure concerns, not a fixable positioning problem
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If interpreting as personal feedback: Are you reducing comp expectations or title targets in response, when the correct response may be sector targeting adjustment?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If interpreting correctly as structural signal: Have you redirected search toward management track, advisory, or consulting roles where this signal is less prevalent?

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your current work authorization status in Canada — PGWP, Canadian PR, employer-specific permit, or none?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether LMIA is required and which segment of the PM job market is accessible, which is the single most important structural constraint in Canadian PM job searching
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If PGWP: confirm expiry date and months remaining; calculate whether CEC 12-month threshold is achievable within PGWP validity
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If no valid authorization: determine whether LMIA, GTS, ICT, or a new study/work permit is the most viable pathway before job searching

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you want to be evaluated on your own product judgment, or on the quality of product judgment you develop in others?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: The core motivational orientation that separates the two tracks — personal expertise identity vs. multiplier identity
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If own judgment: Ask whether they are comfortable with the political influence work of IC — driving outcomes without formal authority across their entire career
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If others' judgment: Ask whether they have experienced the full range of people management work, including sustained underperformer development and difficult termination decisions, not just high-signal mentoring moments

diagnostic_questions.question: Can you name the specific companies or roles that are currently closed to you that would open with an MBA?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the MBA is solving a concrete access problem or a vague career anxiety
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Are those companies currently actively recruiting MBAs into PM roles, or is that pipeline based on pre-2022 data?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: What specifically do you believe is blocking your career progression, and is it actually a credential problem or a skill/network/positioning problem?

diagnostic_questions.question: Does your track record include building products from zero, or primarily scaling existing ones?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the person qualifies for EIR roles and has the founding-relevant credibility that VC firms and early-stage companies look for
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: How recently did you do this, and can you articulate the specific decisions that created success from scratch?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Which of your target pivot paths still apply given this gap, and how will you get 0-to-1 experience before making the move?

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the level code for this role, and what is the next level code above it?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the company can articulate its own leveling structure clearly and whether the PM knows how to navigate it
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What are the stated promotion criteria and typical time-to-promo from this level to the next?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Treat this as a red flag — companies without clear level codes often have opaque promotion processes that favor incumbents over new hires

diagnostic_questions.question: If you subtract equity entirely, does the base salary cover your monthly fixed obligations?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you are gambling with money you need versus money you can afford to lose — this is the foundational risk calibration question
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Then equity is upside — proceed to evaluate the equity structure (dilution, liquidation preferences, exercise window) as a bonus, not as compensation
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: This is a disqualifying condition unless you have significant savings or other income — the offer is asking you to take on financial risk you cannot absorb

diagnostic_questions.question: In the last 6 months, did your scope of decisions expand or contract?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the current environment is offering growth or pulling back; contraction without explanation is an org signal, not a skill signal
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What specifically expanded — is it more ambiguity, more stakeholders, or just more volume of the same work?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Was the contraction explained? If not, who owns the scope that used to be yours?

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your job satisfaction score right now on a 1-10 scale, and what was it six months ago?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you're experiencing a stable situation, a recoverable dip, or a sustained decline that signals structural misfit
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If it's been below 7 for six months: what specifically do you believe will change it, and what is the concrete plan?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If it's stable around 8: what would it take to push it higher, and is that possible in your current role?

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you currently executing against scope that was defined for you, or are you identifying and defining new areas of opportunity yourself?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Which career stage you are actually operating in, regardless of your title — Stage 1 executes against defined scope, Stage 2 defines the scope
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If defining your own scope: are you also making the case for why it is the right area, or are you still seeking approval for the direction?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If executing against defined scope: is this because the organization hasn't given you the opportunity, or because you haven't sought it out?

diagnostic_questions.question: Can you describe the strategic framework for your product area — including target markets, key pain points, and why you are betting on your current approach over alternatives?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the PM has internalized strategic ownership or is executing against someone else's direction
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Who authored that framework — did you create it, or were you handed it? Have you secured executive alignment on it?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Do you know who owns the strategy for your area? What would it take for you to develop and own it?

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you received the same promotional feedback across more than one review cycle without it changing?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the block is a genuine skill gap (feedback would evolve as you develop) or a structural/political ceiling (feedback stays static because the real issue isn't developmental)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Ask your manager directly whether there is a role to be promoted into — distinguish skill gap from headcount constraint
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Treat the feedback as genuine and build a specific action plan with your manager to close the named gaps

diagnostic_questions.question: Has your scope — the actual decision authority and surface area of your work — expanded in the last 12–18 months?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the constraint on career progress is a skill gap (you haven't demonstrated readiness for more scope) or an organizational ceiling (the org structurally cannot give you more scope regardless of performance)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Is that scope expansion visible to the people who make promotion decisions, or is it happening informally?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Have you had explicit conversations with your manager about what would need to be true for you to take on more scope, or are you waiting for it to happen organically?

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your citizenship — Canadian, US/Mexican, or other nationality?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines TN visa eligibility and therefore the viability and timeline of the Canada → US career path, which changes the long-term strategic value of pursuing Canadian PR
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If Canadian citizen: TN to US is immediately available; Canada → US path is 1–2 years, not 5+
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If Indian, Chinese, or other non-North American national: map out citizenship timeline; evaluate H-1B lottery and EB-1A as parallel paths to US

diagnostic_questions.question: In the past three months, what energized you more: solving a hard product problem independently, or unblocking or developing a teammate?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Revealed preference over stated preference — what actually produces energy in daily work rather than what sounds appealing in the abstract
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If problem-solving: Confirm IC orientation and probe whether they have a domain they want to go deep on for the next decade
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If developing teammates: Distinguish whether this is informal mentoring energy or genuine sustained people development appetite — ask about the last time they had to manage someone through a performance issue

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your current employer and compensation level?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you're already inside the recruiting ecosystem MBA candidates are trying to enter, and what your true opportunity cost is
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If at FAANG or top-tier tech: the MBA likely returns you to where you are — what specific outcome justifies the $400K–$500K opportunity cost?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If at a non-top-tier employer: does your compensation and trajectory make the break-even calculation work, and is MBA the specific key or are other factors blocking the doors you want?

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you published investment theses, market teardowns, or product analyses publicly?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the person has established external credibility as a thought leader, which is a prerequisite for VC and consulting pivots
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What audience have these reached, and have any VCs or founders engaged with them?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: What is preventing you from starting now, while still employed, and how long until you would have a meaningful body of work?

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the total compensation for this offer, and how does it compare to the levels.fyi median for this level at this company?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the company is offering within its own band or soft-downleveling by underpaying relative to the stated title
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Confirm the comp is at or above median; if significantly above, understand why (competing offer, specialized skills, or org urgency)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Probe whether the lower comp reflects a lower actual level than the title suggests, or a company-wide compensation issue

diagnostic_questions.question: What are your fixed financial obligations right now — mortgage or rent, dependents, debt service?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Your actual risk tolerance capacity, which changes the entire startup vs. Big Tech calculus regardless of stated preferences
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If obligations are significant, startup base salary risk becomes a real financial exposure, not just career risk — weight Big Tech's compensation predictability much higher
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If obligations are minimal (early career, no dependents, renting), startup financial risk is manageable — learning velocity and scope become the primary decision variables

diagnostic_questions.question: Can you name 3 decisions you made in the last month that your manager doesn't know about?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether real ownership exists — decisions that don't require reporting up signal actual authority; inability to name any means the ownership is thinner than the title suggests
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Are those decisions consequential — do they have real stakes and real feedback loops?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Is this because you escalate by habit or because the org expects escalation? Both are diagnostic but require different fixes

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the scale of what you are building — a feature, a product, a business, or an organization?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether your current scope matches the stage of career you're targeting and what the actual gap is
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If you're building at the right stage: what behaviors from the previous stage are you still holding onto that are limiting you?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If you're building below your target stage: is that a skill gap or an org ceiling preventing scope expansion?

diagnostic_questions.question: When you make a significant decision, do you share the alternatives you considered and the reasoning behind your choice — or do you present the conclusion?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you are actively building or passively assuming trust — invisible judgment cannot generate the credibility required for senior-level autonomy
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If sharing reasoning: are decision-makers able to see your judgment clearly, or is the framing still output-focused?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If presenting conclusions only: have you received feedback that leaders want to be brought in earlier or want to understand your thinking process?

diagnostic_questions.question: When you last brought a problem to your manager, did you come with a proposed approach or just the problem?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the PM is demonstrating autonomous thinking or dependency in upward communication
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What was your manager's response — did they adjust your proposal or redirect you entirely? This reveals how much strategic trust exists.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Is this a habit or a one-off? What stopped you from forming a view first?

diagnostic_questions.question: Can your manager describe your last six months of impact specifically and compellingly without your help?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether your impact is legible enough to survive a calibration conversation you're not present for
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Your visibility is sufficient — focus on scope, champion, and structural factors
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Impact legibility is your most urgent gap — build a habit of proactively surfacing wins and framing them in business terms

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you know specifically what gap your manager would say exists between your current level and the next?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you have activated the partnership approach to promotion or are relying on hope; also reveals whether your manager is functioning as an ally or a ceiling
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you made progress against that specific gap in the last review cycle, and does your manager know it?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: What has prevented you from having that conversation — discomfort, belief that the answer is obvious, or lack of access to your manager?

diagnostic_questions.question: Does your current or most recent employer have a Canadian legal entity?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: If yes, Intra-Company Transfer (ICT C-12 exemption) may be available, which is LMIA-exempt and significantly faster than any external hiring pathway
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Determine whether the Canadian entity is large enough to support an ICT transfer and whether the PM role has a Canadian equivalent; engage HR on ICT process
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Rule out ICT; assess Global Talent Stream eligibility based on NOC code of target PM role as next best LMIA-expedited option

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you need or want the flexibility to work at companies outside large tech (startups, mid-size, different geographies)?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the structural job market constraint of the IC track (10–15% of roles, concentrated at large tech) is a material life constraint or not
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If yes to flexibility: Strongly reconsider IC track or explicitly map which Staff/Principal roles exist in target companies and geographies before committing
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If content at large tech: IC track market constraint is less binding; shift analysis to intrinsic fit questions

diagnostic_questions.question: What type of product role are you targeting — technical/B2B or consumer/generalist?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether MBA credentials are valued or discounted by hiring managers in your target domain
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If technical/B2B: MBA may signal career pivot away from domain depth — have you verified that MBA holders are competitive in your target roles?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If consumer/generalist: MBA is more relevant — research whether your specific target companies still run active MBA PM recruiting programs post-2022

diagnostic_questions.question: Can you name the specific market gap or thesis that makes you want to found a company?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the founding interest is driven by a genuine, defensible insight or by dissatisfaction with the current role — which predicts very different outcomes
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you validated this thesis with potential customers, and have you identified who would co-found with you?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: The desire to found may be about escaping rather than building; explore whether a different pivot (CoS, EIR, new company PM role) addresses the root cause

diagnostic_questions.question: Who has final override authority over the roadmap and prioritization for this role?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: The real scope and autonomy of the role, which can differ dramatically from what the title implies
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If the answer is 'you do,' map this to a staff or principal equivalent scope regardless of title
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If the answer is 'the CEO' or 'a more senior PM,' the role has less scope than the title implies

diagnostic_questions.question: What specific skills, network, and financial position do you want to have in 5 years?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the person has a concrete target state or is evaluating offers in a vacuum — without this, any comparison is noise
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Map each offer's likely outcome against the 5-year target — which path creates more of the prerequisites you've identified?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: The decision cannot be made well until this is defined — spend time on the 5-year vision before evaluating either offer on its merits

diagnostic_questions.question: What specific feedback has been consistent across more than one manager or review cycle?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Multi-source consistent feedback is almost always a real skill gap; inconsistent or politically-colored feedback is usually an org signal
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Can you identify specific behaviors a more senior PM exhibits that you don't yet have? If yes, this is a skill gap — stay and fix it
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Has any feedback felt arbitrary or shifted depending on political context? If yes, this is an org signal, not a skill gap

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you primarily built your career at large companies, small companies, or a mix?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Which instincts you've developed (process navigation vs. radical ownership) and which are likely underdeveloped
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If large companies only: can you point to a time you had radical ownership with no process to rely on?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If startups only: can you point to a time you built alignment across many stakeholders without direct authority?

diagnostic_questions.question: Can you name the key stakeholders and gatekeepers in your organization and articulate what they actually care about — as opposed to what they say they care about?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you have developed organizational dynamics literacy, which is required at Stage 2 and above to move work through the organization
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If yes: are you actively using this understanding to get ahead of resistance and build coalitions before escalations?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If no: are you relying on official processes as your primary model for how decisions get made?

diagnostic_questions.question: Can you name a recent decision where the right answer genuinely depended on context, and articulate what the conditions were?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the PM can reason in conditional logic versus applying rigid frameworks or defaulting to single answers
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Were you able to communicate those conditions to stakeholders clearly, or did you resolve the ambiguity prematurely to appear decisive?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Do you tend to resolve ambiguous decisions quickly? Who do you defer to when the answer isn't clear?

diagnostic_questions.question: Who specifically is advocating for you in the calibration room, and what is their actual organizational influence?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you have real political cover in the decision-making process or only the appearance of it
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Maintain the relationship and keep your champion updated on your impact narrative
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Identify who actually influences calibration outcomes at your level and invest in building a real relationship with them

diagnostic_questions.question: When you evaluate a new role, do you explicitly separate what you find energizing about the work from what makes it sound impressive to others?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the person is using the Tablestakes–Ego–Joy framework or conflating ego satisfaction with genuine fit; reveals susceptibility to taking roles that sound good but produce stagnation
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What specifically did you identify in the joy category that you cannot get from your current role?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Can you articulate what you find genuinely energizing about product work that is independent of how it looks to your peers or recruiters?

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you optimizing for maximum PM career scope and compensation, or for immigration security and lifestyle stability?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Reveals which geography and employer type the candidate should prioritize — these goals favor fundamentally different career paths in Canada vs. US
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If scope and comp: Canada is appropriate for early-career base and PR, but US transition should be planned for mid-career principal/director level
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If stability and lifestyle: Canadian PM market at major banks or established tech companies is well-suited; accept comp ceiling as part of the tradeoff explicitly

diagnostic_questions.question: Is reaching VP or CPO level a realistic goal you are actively pursuing, or an aspirational possibility?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the higher compensation ceiling of the management track at VP+ is a real decision factor or a theoretical one that should not drive the choice
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If realistic and active: Management track comp advantage at VP+ becomes a legitimate factor; assess whether you have the people leadership appetite to sustain the path
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If aspirational only: Remove comp ceiling as a decision factor; the comp difference at Director level is modest (~$55K), and the role content difference is immediate and large

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you a non-US candidate lacking US work authorization or a US recruiting network?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the MBA's value proposition is primarily about H-1B sponsorship and campus recruiting access — a structurally different and stronger case than for US citizens
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: This is one of the strongest legitimate use cases — validate that your target companies sponsor H-1B through MBA hiring and research visa pathway specifics
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If US citizen with existing credentials: the visa/network access argument doesn't apply — return to whether a specific credential gap or access gap justifies the cost

diagnostic_questions.question: How comfortable are you with outcome feedback that takes years rather than weeks?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the person's motivation and decision-making systems are compatible with VC or founding, where short-term feedback loops are absent
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Can you describe a past experience where you sustained conviction and quality judgment over a long period without external validation?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: VC and founding are likely to be psychologically misaligned; explore pivots with faster feedback (consulting, operator leadership)

diagnostic_questions.question: What level did the last person in this role hold, and why did they leave?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the company is trying to backfill with someone appropriately leveled or is attempting to hire above the role's actual scope
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If the previous person was at a lower level, ask why the company is now hiring higher
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If the company can't answer, it may indicate poor people-process discipline or that the role is newly created without clear scope definition

diagnostic_questions.question: Can the startup founder tell you the current MRR, customer churn rate, burn rate, and months of runway without hedging?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the startup has the financial transparency and stability that makes the risk calculable, and whether the founder is operating with real customer traction or primarily vision
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Proceed to evaluate liquidation preferences, exercise window length, and dilution history from prior funding rounds
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: This is a red flag — a founder who talks more about vision than customers or can't give specific runway numbers is either uninformed or evasive, both of which are disqualifying

diagnostic_questions.question: If you left tomorrow, what would be missing that you haven't learned yet?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the current role still has extractable value; if the answer is 'nothing significant,' staying is likely a comfort decision, not a growth decision
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Is that learning actually available in the current role — is there scope and opportunity to acquire it, or is it theoretically available but structurally inaccessible?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Have you been honest with yourself about whether you're avoiding something rather than completing something?

diagnostic_questions.question: Who in your network advocates for you in rooms you're not in?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you have sponsors (not just mentors) and whether your advancement is being actively championed
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If you have sponsors: are they in the right rooms — the ones where promotion, hiring, and opportunity decisions are made?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If you have no sponsors: is that because you haven't built the right relationships, or because you haven't done work visible enough to advocate for?

diagnostic_questions.question: If asked in an executive meeting, could you articulate why your product area matters to the company's strategy in a way that is both accurate and energizing?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you have done the strategic alignment work required at senior levels — PMs who cannot answer this are invisible in resource allocation decisions
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If yes: have you actually communicated this in contexts where it would be heard, or only in your own planning?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If no: is this a gap in your thinking or a gap in your communication of thinking you've already done?

diagnostic_questions.question: How much of your working week is spent on strategic work versus reactive execution work?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the PM has structural conditions that allow senior-level behavior to develop, or is trapped in execution mode
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Is that time protected on your calendar, or does it happen opportunistically? Opportunistic strategy time is effectively no strategy time.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Have you ever explicitly blocked time for strategy? What would you need to stop doing to create that space?

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you explicitly told your manager that you want to be promoted and discussed timing directly?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether your manager has a clear urgency signal from you or is operating on assumption of contentment
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Confirm your manager has a concrete plan and timeline, not just acknowledgment
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Have this conversation immediately — the absence of this signal is likely deprioritizing your case in competitive cycles

diagnostic_questions.question: Can you name the people who will be in your next promotion calibration, and would they be able to describe your specific contributions unprompted?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the person's impact is visible to the actual decision-makers, or whether they are relying on organic recognition in a system with documented presentation bias
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: How did you ensure that visibility — was it deliberate narration or high-visibility presentations, and is it sustainable?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: What is your plan to make your work legible to those people before the next calibration cycle?

diagnostic_questions.question: How many months of continuous NOC TEER 1 Canadian work experience have you accrued?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines proximity to the 12-month CEC eligibility threshold for Express Entry PR, which is the most actionable immigration milestone for PM candidates on PGWP
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If 12+ months: assess current Express Entry CRS score and determine whether CEC draw is feasible in current cycle
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If less than 12 months: calculate exact months remaining; ensure current role's NOC code qualifies and that employment is continuous

diagnostic_questions.question: How do you experience stress — is political influence without formal authority more draining, or is direct accountability for other people's performance more draining?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Which track's stress profile the person has more sustained coping capacity for, since both tracks carry significant but structurally different stress types
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If political influence is more draining: Management track stress profile may be a better fit, but probe whether formal people accountability (firing, sustained underperformer management) is genuinely comfortable
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If people accountability is more draining: IC track stress profile is likely a better long-term fit; ensure they understand that influencing without authority is a permanent IC career condition, not a phase

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your target role 5–7 years out — CPO track, GM/COO track, or strategy/consulting-adjacent leadership?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether MBA is structurally expected in your target destination or largely irrelevant to it
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If GM/COO/strategy track: MBA provides a business generalist toolkit that is more commonly expected — validate by checking backgrounds of people currently in those roles
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If CPO track at tech company: MBA is often not needed — research CPO backgrounds at your target companies and assess whether MBA is a common pathway

diagnostic_questions.question: Is there a specific executive you want to learn from, or do you want a CoS role generically?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether a CoS pursuit is strategically motivated (learn from a specific person, bridge to a defined next role) or status-motivated (proximity to power without a plan)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you mapped what you would learn from this person that you cannot get elsewhere, and what the CoS-to-next-role transition looks like?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: CoS without a specific learning or transition rationale is likely to result in 12–24 months of unclear career positioning

diagnostic_questions.question: Is this move increasing total compensation by more than 20%?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the financial upside is sufficient to justify any title or scope tradeoff
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: A 20%+ comp increase with brand upgrade is likely worth a title downlevel; evaluate scope and upgrade path
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If comp is flat or declining and the title is the same or lower, the move has no compensating factors and the decision rests entirely on scope and future optionality

diagnostic_questions.question: At the Big Tech role, what has this specific team shipped in the last 12 months — can you name three products?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the team is actually shipping or is in a planning/reorganization holding pattern — a strong brand doesn't mean this particular team is executing
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Probe the manager's decision-making style and the promotion trajectory (time-to-promo at your level in this specific org)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: High turnover or inability to name recent shipped work suggests either a reorganization in progress or a low-momentum team — probe why the role exists before proceeding

diagnostic_questions.question: Does your current manager understand what you want to do next, and can they describe a path to it?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether effective advocacy is possible; a manager who can't articulate your path can't fight for you even if they want to
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Can they name two people who have made that transition — is there evidence the path is real, not aspirational?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Is this because you haven't told them, or because they don't have the organizational knowledge or capital to know?

diagnostic_questions.question: When did you last feel genuinely incompetent at something in your job?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you're on a real learning curve or have settled into a comfortable competence plateau
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If recently: are you treating that discomfort as information about growth or as a signal you made a mistake?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If not recently: what does that tell you about the growth potential of your current role?

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you collected 360-degree feedback recently, and do the people you escalate with or disagree with describe you as constructive and collaborative?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Your collaborative reputation, which executives use heavily as a signal for who gets expanded scope — being tolerated versus being actively sought out is a significant career differentiator
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If positive reputation: are leaders actively pulling you into cross-functional work, or is the collaboration reactive only?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If reputation is unclear or negative: is the feedback about style (defensiveness, self-interest) or substance (disagreement on direction)?

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the 2–3 year vision for your product area, and can you show how this quarter's work connects to it?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the PM thinks in strategic themes and long arcs or in sprint cycles and feature lists
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Did you communicate that vision to your team and leadership? Is it documented in a form others can reference and hold you to?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Do you know if a vision exists at a level above you? If so, why haven't you translated it into your area?

diagnostic_questions.question: Is your current scope materially different from what it was 12 months ago?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you are demonstrating next-level performance or repeating the same level of work on a longer tenure
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Assess whether that scope expansion is visible and attributed to you in the org's perception
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Scope stagnation is a leading indicator that you will not have evidence to support a promotion case — identify what you can proactively own

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have a clear picture of what you want your career to look like in five years, including what skills, scope, decisions, and relationships you will need?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the person is making day-to-day decisions with a directional long-term view or optimizing purely for the next 6–12 month promotion cycle
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Are your current project choices and relationship investments actually aligned with that five-year picture?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Are your current career decisions being made primarily by reacting to what is available or what your manager assigns, rather than by a proactive strategy?

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you targeting Canadian-headquartered companies, Canadian offices of US companies, or both?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Canadian offices of US companies (Amazon CA, Google CA) often offer stronger comp and global product scope, but hire fewer PMs; Canadian HQ companies offer more seats but smaller product scope and lower comp
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If US company Canadian offices: prepare for fewer total roles, more competitive process, and potentially global product context in interviews
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If Canadian HQ only: calibrate comp expectations to Canadian market rates and prepare for regulated-environment or domestic-market product cases

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you making this decision because a specific opportunity was offered, or because you have proactively sought this path?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the decision is reactive (high failure risk) or deliberate (lower failure risk), since the most common failure pattern is accepting management as a promotion offer rather than choosing it as a different job
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If reactive — offer was made: Slow down the decision; reframe explicitly as 'which different job do I want' rather than 'do I accept this promotion'
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If proactively sought: Validate that the proactive choice was based on the actual daily work content of management, not on perceived seniority signals or comp ceiling assumptions

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you calculated the full opportunity cost including lost salary and missed promotion cycles, not just tuition?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate is reasoning about true cost or only the visible tuition figure
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Does the expected comp uplift from MBA exceed that full figure over your remaining career horizon?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Run the actual math: 2-year M7 cost (~$247K) + 2 years of foregone salary at your current level + value of missed promotion cycle — does any realistic post-MBA outcome exceed this?

diagnostic_questions.question: How many genuine relationships do you currently have with people in your target pivot domain (VCs, founders, operators)?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the person has the network infrastructure for a viable pivot or is starting from zero, which dramatically affects timeline and probability
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Are these relationships warm enough that you could ask for an introduction, a referral, or honest feedback about your fit?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Network-building in the target domain should begin immediately and run in parallel with current role; cold pivots without network take 2–3x longer

diagnostic_questions.question: Where are you in your career — 0–5 years, 5–10 years, or 10+ years of PM experience?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Which phase of the learning vs. stability vs. credentialism tradeoff you're in — the right answer genuinely differs by career stage
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If early (0–5): learning velocity dominates the decision, and meaningful startup scope may outweigh a Big Tech role with narrow initial scope
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If mid (5–10): assess whether Big Tech has produced a real learning plateau; if late (10+): Big Tech credentialism matters more for senior hires and startup transitions become harder

diagnostic_questions.question: When did you last surprise yourself — do something in your current role you didn't know you could do?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the role is still at the growth edge; inability to recall a recent surprise is a strong signal the role is no longer developing new capabilities
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Is that happening regularly, or was it a one-time event 18 months ago?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Is the absence of surprise because the role is too comfortable, or because external factors (org structure, limited scope) removed the conditions for growth?

diagnostic_questions.question: Before your last major career move, did you test the hypothesis through smaller experiments?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the person applies product thinking to their own career or makes binary leaps based on unvalidated assumptions
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If yes: what did you learn from those experiments that changed or confirmed your decision?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If no: what assumption did you make that you wish you had tested first?

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you preparing for promotion by developing skills, or by seeking expanded scope and demonstrating impact at that scope?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you understand the actual mechanism of promotion — skill development is necessary but not sufficient; scope and demonstrated impact are what actually drive promotion decisions
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If pursuing scope: have you made the case to your manager for why you should own expanded areas, and what was the response?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If focused on skills: do you know which specific scope expansions would be available to you if you sought them?

diagnostic_questions.question: When you look at people who have been promoted in your org recently, do you understand the narrative that got them there?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you understand what your org actually rewards versus what it says it rewards — the gap between these is where promotions are won or lost
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Assess whether your own work and narrative match those patterns
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Study recent promotions more carefully — talk to those people or their managers to understand the actual criteria in practice

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have peer relationships outside your company — built before you needed them — with people at similar career stages who give you honest feedback?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the person has pattern recognition across organizations to distinguish company-specific dysfunction from industry norms, and whether they have the network infrastructure to navigate future transitions
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have those peers helped you identify something about your situation that you would have misread if you had only internal information?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Are you currently interpreting your company's dynamics through only internal reference points, which may cause you to misattribute org ceilings as personal skill gaps or vice versa?

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your financial runway if your pivot takes 18 months to generate income?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the person can make quality decisions during a transition or will be forced into suboptimal choices by financial pressure
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you modeled the minimum income you need vs. the likely income trajectory of your target pivot in its first two years?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: The pivot plan needs to either include a bridge (advisory work, part-time consulting) or be delayed until runway is sufficient

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the exercise window on the startup options — standard 90 days or an extended window?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you will be able to afford to leave the company if the role stops being right for you, and the actual cost of the optionality you're accepting
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If extended (5+ years): the exit trap is much less severe — you can leave without immediately paying 20–50% of annual salary to preserve options
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If 90 days: model explicitly what it would cost you to exercise at current strike price and whether you could afford it — if not, you are accepting a golden handcuff

diagnostic_questions.question: What are the last two big decisions the team made and why?

diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Were those decisions made by the PM or by a committee — who actually had the call?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Vague or evasive answers signal that decisions are made elsewhere; this is a strong signal to walk away from the role

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you know whether there is current headcount and budget for a promotion at your target level this cycle?

diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Either get clarity from your manager or treat this cycle as a development cycle and begin evaluating the external market in parallel
