psychological_barriers.expert_move: Ask them to apply to three comparable roles externally and see what happens; actual market feedback is the only antidote to inflated self-assessment
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_互联网人跳槽的注意事项有哪些.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: PM who has hit a promotion ceiling despite meeting all documented criteria they were told to meet
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Attribution error combined with institutional trust — the PM trusted the official rubric as the complete picture and now experiences the outcome as arbitrary or unfair rather than diagnosable
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Venting about process unfairness, considering leaving the company without diagnosing the actual gap (often internal visibility), or doubling down on craft improvement when the real gap is political
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Ask: 'Who outside your immediate team could walk a panel through your impact right now?' If the answer is 'nobody,' the problem is visibility, not performance — these require completely different interventions
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_产品经理应该如何进行职业规划.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Person asking whether PM career advancement is 'difficult' in general
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Outcome uncertainty avoidance — seeking reassurance that the new path has a predictable ceiling before committing, rather than evaluating fit
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Abstract questions about career trajectory ('is it hard to get promoted?') instead of concrete questions about what skills drive promotion and whether the person is developing them
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Redirect from 'is this path hard?' to 'what specifically drives advancement on this path, and do you have or can you build those things?' This surfaces actionable self-assessment instead of generic reassurance.
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_产品经理的职业发展_岗位晋升方面怎么样_是否很困难.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: PM with 3–4 years of experience has not hit expected milestones (no owned product line, no success story) and is asking 'what should I do'
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Sunk cost + identity protection; avoiding the diagnosis that the years invested haven't produced the outcomes expected
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Asks vague strategic questions, seeks external validation, looks for a framework that will make the current path feel like it's working
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Force the concrete audit: 'Name a product you owned and the data that moved because of your decisions.' If this cannot be answered, the question isn't 'what should I do next' but 'what ownership have I been avoiding acquiring and why'
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_产品经理的职业生涯规划是怎么样的.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: PM at 5-8 years asks which track they should choose — management or specialist — framing it as an urgent either/or decision
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Identity anxiety combined with external status pressure; management is perceived as the socially validated path, creating pressure to choose it regardless of fit
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Choosing management because it seems like progression, not because of genuine preference assessment; framing the question as 'which is better' rather than 'which fits me'
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Shift from 'which is better' to 'what do I actually enjoy doing daily' — probe whether they prefer influencing people or solving product problems, and whether they have the prerequisite traits for their stated preference
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_产品经理要如何晋升_有哪些晋升路径.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Senior PM describing their situation as 'stable' while simultaneously noting they haven't changed scope in 2-3 years and are avoiding visibility
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Sunk cost + loss aversion: the person has invested years in a company and fears that any change (internal or external) risks losing the accumulated status; mistaking inertia for stability
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Rationalizes staying as strategic ('I know this company, I have relationships here') while avoiding the harder question of whether the current role is building any new capability
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Ask: if your current role disappeared tomorrow, what specifically would you point to from the last 2 years that makes you more valuable than before? If the answer is unclear, the 'stability' is actually risk accumulation.
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_那些35岁以上的产品经理都去做什么了.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Question: 'What do I say when they ask about sponsorship on the call?' (267 upvotes on the question itself, indicating widespread anxiety at this specific moment)
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Anticipatory rejection anxiety; the candidate has successfully gotten to the call but now fears the sponsorship conversation will undo all progress; the preparation gap creates paralysis
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidates avoid getting on calls they could have gotten; or get on calls and handle the sponsorship conversation poorly because they have no prepared framing
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Treat the sponsorship conversation as a separate skill to prepare for; draft a 2-3 sentence framing that leads with your value and OPT timeline, not with the sponsorship ask; practice it before the first call
psychological_barriers._source: cscareerquestions_cold_email_got_me_my_job_actual_template_that_work.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Feeling unable to search for new roles while still employed without feeling guilty or disloyal
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Identity enmeshment with current employer; leaving feels like betrayal rather than a normal career event
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Person delays job search, stays in a suboptimal role too long, or feels they must quit first before looking
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe: 'You are managing your personal brand, not being disloyal. Your employer is simultaneously managing their talent pipeline. Both are normal.'
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_互联网人跳槽的注意事项有哪些.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Senior PM (5+ years) feeling like they should still be investing primarily in product craft and methodology
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Competence safety bias — foundational skill-building feels measurable and safe; business domain commitment and external visibility feel ambiguous and risky
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Continuing to invest in tools, frameworks, and methodology at mid/senior career instead of building domain depth or external reputation — staying in '0-1 mode' mentally while expecting '10-100 outcomes'
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Name the stage mismatch explicitly: 'The investment that got you here is not the investment that gets you to the next level — the formula changes by phase'
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_产品经理应该如何进行职业规划.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Early-career PM (1–2 years) is watching peers join startups and feeling pressure to do the same
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: FOMO and social comparison anxiety; overweighting visible peer outcomes (survivorship bias in action)
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: PM rushes to join any startup, prioritizing the perception of boldness over fit; cannot articulate what specific skills the startup will build that their current role won't
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Ask: 'What specific outcome are you trying to achieve by joining a startup, and why can't you achieve it where you are?' If the answer is about perception or peer comparison rather than a concrete skill or ownership gap, the decision is being driven by anxiety not strategy
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_产品经理的职业生涯规划是怎么样的.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: PM describes doing post-defense retrospective and feeling regret about answers they gave, saying they 'missed their chance'
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Perfectionism and counterfactual fixation; the gap between ideal performance and actual performance is experienced as failure rather than as normal variance
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Excessive self-criticism after each defense; reluctance to attempt again; framing sub-optimal answers as disqualifying rather than as development data
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Normalize the gap: even experienced PMs who have passed many promotions still feel they answered imperfectly in retrospect. The standard is 'better than last time,' not 'perfect.' Treat each retrospective as input to the next attempt, not as a verdict on this one
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_产品经理要如何晋升_有哪些晋升路径.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Female PM framing career decisions primarily around family obligations ('已婚有娃') when discussing career stalls or job search difficulty
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Identity conflict between professional ambition and social expectations; may be using family obligations as a face-saving explanation for career stalls that have other causes
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Attributes career ceiling to family situation rather than investigating skill gaps or organizational dynamics; may underinvest in capability development because 'it won't matter anyway given my family situation'
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Separate the diagnosis from the constraint: first establish clearly whether the gap is skill-based or org-based, then assess family constraints as a separate decision variable. Don't let one explain away the other.
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_那些35岁以上的产品经理都去做什么了.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Feeling rushed to accept an offer because savings are low or current situation is intolerable
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Scarcity mindset — economic pressure narrows cognitive bandwidth and inflates the apparent value of the first available escape
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Accepting offers without negotiating, joining roles that don't meet stated criteria, and regretting it within months
psychological_barriers.expert_move: The financial buffer prescription (2 months savings minimum) is the structural fix; without it, advise building the buffer before resigning rather than trying to decide well under pressure
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_互联网人跳槽的注意事项有哪些.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: PM asks how to get promoted at a company that 'doesn't have the resources of a big tech firm' for guidance
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Institutional comparison anxiety; the belief that without formal support structures, success is less achievable or less legitimate
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Underinvesting in self-advocacy and preparation because the environment feels unsupportive; waiting for institutional guidance rather than proactively seeking peer examples and frameworks
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Identify the two or three people inside your company who have recently passed the promotion you're targeting and treat them as your primary research subjects — internal precedents beat generic frameworks in every case
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_产品经理要如何晋升_有哪些晋升路径.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: PM describing a major career decision (joining a startup, leaving for self-media) in terms of happiness and meaning without any financial sustainability analysis
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Reactance and escapism — after years of high-pressure PM work, the person is so depleted that any alternative feels appealing; conflating relief from current pain with genuine positive value of the alternative
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Makes a major career exit without a financial model; discovers income is 'tight' afterward but maintains the framing of 'I'm happier' to avoid confronting the decision's cost
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Before any exit decision, require a 24-month financial model: what does income look like in months 1, 6, 12, 18, 24 under the new path? Separate the question of 'am I in the wrong current role' from 'is this specific alternative the right move.'
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_那些35岁以上的产品经理都去做什么了.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I have a work permit so I need to explain my immigration status carefully
reframing_moves.reframe: You are not explaining your status — you are eliminating an employer's concern before it becomes a rejection
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the candidate from defensive disclosure to proactive objection removal; changes the emotional register from 'I have to justify myself' to 'I am making your decision easier'
reframing_moves.example_language: 'I hold an open work permit. You do not need to sponsor me or file any applications.'
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestionsCAD_getting_your_first_canadian_tech_job_on_pgwp_what_.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I'm an international student — I need to tell employers about my visa situation and that I'll need sponsorship
reframing_moves.reframe: PGWP is not a burden. You don't need sponsorship. The employer does nothing. Stop using the US framing.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: It separates the PGWP from the US visa-as-burden mental model entirely — rather than softening the liability framing, it eliminates the category of 'liability' altogether
reframing_moves.example_language: 'PGWP is genuinely not a burden to employers' — the framing shift is from 'how do I minimize this obstacle' to 'there is no obstacle'
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestionsCAD_pgwp_job_search_reality_check_what_nobody_tells_yo.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: How do I bring up my visa situation without hurting my chances?
reframing_moves.reframe: Stop treating it as something to survive — treat it as an alignment check. You're not asking for permission; you're establishing whether the role is a mutual fit.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the candidate from a supplicant frame (I need them to accept my flaw) to a professional frame (we are both evaluating fit) — changes both the internal anxiety and the external language
reframing_moves.example_language: 'Just so we're aligned — I'm currently on OPT and authorized to work. I'd need H-1B sponsorship in the future. Is that something [company] does?'
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestions_asking_about_visa_sponsorship_in_job_interviews_th.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I need to be honest about my visa situation upfront so I don't waste anyone's time
reframing_moves.reframe: By the time you've had a conversation, the person is invested in you. Opening with 'I need sponsorship' immediately triggers rejection before they even read your skills.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the frame from 'what is ethical' to 'what is sequentially effective'; reveals that the timing of disclosure, not the disclosure itself, is the variable under the candidate's control
reframing_moves.example_language: 'Opening with I need sponsorship immediately triggers rejection before they even read your skills'
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestions_cold_email_got_me_my_job_actual_template_that_work.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Should I do a PhD at program X or program Y? Which is better for getting into industry?
reframing_moves.reframe: The program ranking question is secondary — what matters is which advisor at either program has placed students at the specific industry labs you're targeting
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the student from a prestige-comparison frame (where rank is the dominant variable) to a placement-pipeline frame (where advisor industry connections are the dominant variable), producing a more actionable evaluation criterion
reframing_moves.example_language: Check LinkedIn for where each advisor's last 5 students interned and ended up — that's the actual signal, not the program's US News ranking
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestions_industry_phd_vs_academic_phd_in_cs_ml_the_real_dif.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: My company broke their promise — what are my options now?
reframing_moves.reframe: The promise was never legally real. The real question is: how many months do you have, and what does your job search calendar need to look like to hit the cap registration window?
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the poster from a backward-looking grievance frame (betrayal, unfairness) to a forward-looking resource allocation frame (time, milestones, deadlines), which is the only frame that produces useful action
reframing_moves.example_language: Verbal promises aren't legally binding for H-1B. Your only real asset right now is the months left on your STEM OPT.
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestions_my_employer_said_they_d_sponsor_h_1b_then_rescinde.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Should I switch jobs? Is now a good time?
reframing_moves.reframe: What do you need to get from your next role — and does your current role have any path to delivering that?
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the question from a binary yes/no timing decision to a goal-clarity exercise; forces the person to articulate what they're optimizing for before evaluating any external option
reframing_moves.example_language: 明确想要在下一份工作得到什么 (Clarify what you want to gain from your next job) — the goal must be explicit before any opportunity can be evaluated
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_互联网人跳槽的注意事项有哪些.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: What career paths are available after 3-5 years as a PM?
reframing_moves.reframe: You already have the baseline skills — the real question is which dimension of depth do you want to build next: industry vertical knowledge, domain specialization, or cross-functional breadth? These require different investments and suit different people.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the PM from passive consumer of available paths to active architect of a deliberate capability investment — converts an anxiety-producing open question into a tractable decision between three concrete options
reframing_moves.example_language: 3-5年的产品经理已经具备了作为产品的基本技能...接下来有三个方向可以突破 (3-5 year PMs already have the foundational skills... the next step is to break through in one of three directions)
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_产品经理工作_3_5_年后有哪些发展路径.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: How do I survive as a PM after 35? / Is product management a dead-end career past mid-life?
reframing_moves.reframe: The question is not 'will the market accept me at 35?' — it is 'how do I make myself more valuable?' The five-factor formula tells you exactly where to invest.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts from external threat (age, market) to internal controllable factors — transforms a scarcity anxiety question into a compounding investment question
reframing_moves.example_language: 每位产品经理应该考虑的是'如何让自己更加值钱'，而不是'中年之后我该怎么办' — What every PM should ask is 'how do I become more valuable,' not 'what do I do after middle age'
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_产品经理应该如何进行职业规划.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Is PM career advancement difficult? What are the prospects?
reframing_moves.reframe: The real question is not whether PM advancement is difficult in general, but whether YOUR core reason for wanting to switch can actually be solved by becoming a PM — and whether you can accept starting over
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the person from seeking external validation about a career path to doing internal diagnostic work about fit and readiness — which is the only analysis that actually matters for their specific decision
reframing_moves.example_language: 你需要自己不断深思，找到自己最核心的原因，思考转行是否能解决这个原因 (You need to keep reflecting deeply, find your single core reason, and think about whether switching careers can actually resolve that reason)
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_产品经理的职业发展_岗位晋升方面怎么样_是否很困难.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Is product management a youth job? Will I age out of this career?
reframing_moves.reframe: The question isn't whether PM favors youth — it's whether your value is coming from novelty (which youth has) or from domain expertise and execution depth (which experience builds). The market has already shifted toward valuing the latter.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Moves the PM from a fixed demographic frame (age as destiny) to a dynamic capability frame (what are you building that compounds). It also correctly identifies that the cultural assumption about PM being a youth job is historically specific to a period that has passed
reframing_moves.example_language: '商业逐渐回归本质，创新不再是互联网公司所追求的' — business is returning to fundamentals; innovation is no longer what internet companies are chasing
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_产品经理的职业生涯规划是怎么样的.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: B2B promotion is harder because I don't have big user numbers or C2C-style metrics to show
reframing_moves.reframe: The question isn't 'do I have the right metrics?' — it's 'can I prove two things: the value I created, and why I specifically was necessary to create it?'
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the PM from metric-comparison anxiety to argument construction; makes the problem tractable by replacing an uncontrollable variable (scale) with two controllable ones (narrative and evidence)
reframing_moves.example_language: B端晋升答辩的本质，只在于两点：如何有效呈现自己的工作价值，为什么做出这些价值的一定得是你而不是别人
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_产品经理要如何晋升_有哪些晋升路径.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Will I be replaced by cheaper, younger talent at 35 since they can do the same PM tasks faster?
reframing_moves.reframe: You are asking the wrong question — the question is whether you have transitioned your value from execution to judgment and leverage. If you haven't, the fear is correct. If you have, it's irrelevant.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the locus of control from external threat (younger talent) to internal capability (your own development trajectory); turns an anxiety spiral into an actionable diagnostic
reframing_moves.example_language: '如果你有这样的想法，那只能说明，你对这个职业还有很深的误解' — if you're thinking this way, it only shows you have a deep misunderstanding of what the career actually is
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_那些35岁以上的产品经理都去做什么了.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I'm not getting responses — I need to apply to more jobs
reframing_moves.reframe: A 2% response rate is a channel diagnosis, not a qualifications diagnosis — the question is whether referrals produce a different rate from the same candidate
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Breaks the volume-as-solution loop by introducing a falsifiable test; if referrals produce 30% vs. 2% cold, the candidate's qualifications are not the variable — the channel is
reframing_moves.example_language: 'The 30% referral response rate vs. 2% cold is real. This is a channel problem, not a you problem.'
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestionsCAD_getting_your_first_canadian_tech_job_on_pgwp_what_.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I just need to work for 1 year and then I can apply for PR through CEC
reframing_moves.reframe: The 1 year must be in a NOC TEER 0–3 role — and CRS score determines whether you get invited, so language scores and French are inputs you need to be optimizing now, not later
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts from a binary 'wait and apply' mental model to a multi-variable optimization problem where actions taken during the 1-year work period directly affect outcomes
reframing_moves.example_language: 'Make sure you're tracking this is in your NOC code properly' — the reframe surfaces a hidden disqualifier most candidates haven't thought about
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestionsCAD_pgwp_job_search_reality_check_what_nobody_tells_yo.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I got told 'we don't sponsor' so I removed them from my list
reframing_moves.reframe: That answer may have been the recruiter's confusion, not company policy — one clarifying question about OPT vs. H-1B could change the answer entirely
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Moves the candidate from accepting a possibly uninformed answer as final to treating recruiter knowledge as a variable — restores agency and expands the viable job pool
reframing_moves.example_language: 'Does that mean no H-1B petition, or also no STEM OPT extension paperwork? I ask because those are pretty different asks.'
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestions_asking_about_visa_sponsorship_in_job_interviews_th.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I'm trying to get a job — I should ask for a job in my email
reframing_moves.reframe: You're asking for a low-commitment 20 minutes. Every ask is for the next small step only.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Reframes the goal of each touchpoint from 'close the job' to 'advance to the next step'; reduces the psychological friction of the ask for both sender and recipient; makes the strategy feel achievable rather than presumptuous
reframing_moves.example_language: 'Every ask is for the next small step only'
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestions_cold_email_got_me_my_job_actual_template_that_work.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Is a PhD worth it in CS/ML?
reframing_moves.reframe: Worth it for what specific role? The PhD premium is real and large for research scientist roles, and essentially zero for SWE roles — the question is unanswerable without specifying the target
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Forces the poster to decompose a binary credential question into a role-specific ROI question, which is the only frame that produces an actionable answer
reframing_moves.example_language: The PhD premium is real for research roles; it barely exists for SWE roles. Which one are you actually targeting?
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestions_industry_phd_vs_academic_phd_in_cs_ml_the_real_dif.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Should I disclose my visa situation in interviews? It might hurt my chances.
reframing_moves.reframe: Hiding it doesn't help you — it just delays the rejection. Early disclosure screens out employers who won't sponsor and concentrates your time on ones who will.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Reframes disclosure from a vulnerability (increases rejection risk) to a filtering tool (increases efficiency), removing the perceived downside of transparency
reframing_moves.example_language: Honest screening saves everyone time. State your deadline upfront.
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestions_my_employer_said_they_d_sponsor_h_1b_then_rescinde.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I think I'm worth more than my current salary — I should switch for a raise
reframing_moves.reframe: Go look at job postings for your target role right now. What do they require that you don't have yet?
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Replaces inflated self-assessment with external market calibration; the gap revealed is more useful than either the confidence or the anxiety
reframing_moves.example_language: 不怕不识货，就怕货比货 (Don't be afraid of not knowing your worth — be afraid of not comparing yourself to the market)
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_互联网人跳槽的注意事项有哪些.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: How do I get promoted from PM to director?
reframing_moves.reframe: Promotion at the director level is about scope of ownership, not task quality — ask yourself whether you are currently owning outcomes at the product-line level or still at the feature-module level, and whether your org gives you a real path to expand that scope
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Replaces a performance-framing (work harder, produce more) with a structural-framing (scope ownership is the actual promotion lever) — this changes what the PM focuses on and what conversations they have with their manager
reframing_moves.example_language: 从产品经理提升为高级产品经理，将会负责整个支付功能，也就是一条产品线 (moving from PM to Senior PM means owning the entire payment feature set — a full product line)
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_产品经理工作_3_5_年后有哪些发展路径.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I'm a product manager and need to plan my PM career path
reframing_moves.reframe: The PM title is just one vehicle — the underlying skill is commercial problem-solving (discover need → propose solution → drive to launch), which applies in any industry. Plan for the skill, not the title.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Breaks the identity lock on the PM title — opens up a much larger option space and reduces anxiety about PM-specific market dynamics
reframing_moves.example_language: 把产品工作的内核抽象出来，似乎放在任何行业都适用 — Abstract the core of PM work out, and it seems to apply in any industry
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_产品经理应该如何进行职业规划.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: What is the standard career path for a product manager?
reframing_moves.reframe: Before mapping a standard path, you need to know which type of PM you are — because Type A (entrepreneurial), Type B (confident but cautious), and Type C (building competence) should make fundamentally different choices at every stage. There is no universal path.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Prevents the common failure of following a template designed for someone else; forces self-knowledge before strategy. The reframe also gives the person a useful taxonomy to locate themselves in rather than just a vague call for 'self-reflection'
reframing_moves.example_language: '我们都看到的是成功的产品人如何如何，往往会忽略自己想要什么、自己是什么类型的人' — we all see the successful cases; we consistently ignore what we actually want and what type of person we are
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_产品经理的职业生涯规划是怎么样的.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Promotion defense is something I need to pass — it's stressful and I might fail
reframing_moves.reframe: Participating in promotion defense is a forcing function for measuring yourself against the level standard — the diagnostic value exists regardless of the outcome
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Converts a binary pass/fail framing into an always-valuable learning process; removes the psychological cost of attempting and failing by redefining what success means
reframing_moves.example_language: 多参与答辩也会迫使你经常以职级通道标准来检视你的工作，这样也可以知道自己短板所在
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_产品经理要如何晋升_有哪些晋升路径.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I've been doing core product modules for years — I should keep building more module experience to become more senior
reframing_moves.reframe: More modules only gives you quantitative change. The qualitative leap comes from taking your methodology and using it to influence more people — document it, teach it, expand your organizational footprint.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Redefines 'seniority' from breadth of execution to depth of organizational impact; gives the PM a concrete alternative action (methodology output, mentoring) rather than just telling them to 'think more strategically'
reframing_moves.example_language: '继续做其他模块只能给你带来量变，但是对于能力提升不能带来质变' — doing more modules only gives you quantitative change, not qualitative capability growth
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_那些35岁以上的产品经理都去做什么了.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Managers and HR both do hiring — I should contact whoever is most accessible
reframing_moves.reframe: Managers hire because they have a problem to solve. HR screens because they have quotas. Very different conversations.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Replaces a functional description (both involved in hiring) with a motivational description (different incentive structures produce different conversations); gives the candidate a clear targeting criterion based on who has a problem the candidate can solve
reframing_moves.example_language: 'Managers hire because they have a problem to solve. HR screens because they have quotas.'
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestions_cold_email_got_me_my_job_actual_template_that_work.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: How do I make sure I'm making progress in my career?
reframing_moves.reframe: Treat job requirements as a skill progression map — assign yourself concrete milestones from real postings and track completion like a game
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Converts abstract career anxiety into specific, actionable, measurable tasks; the game metaphor reduces emotional weight and increases motivation
reframing_moves.example_language: 经验条化 (experience-bar-ification) — make your career progress as visible and trackable as a game level bar
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_互联网人跳槽的注意事项有哪些.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: What level requirements do I need to meet to get promoted to the next PM level?
reframing_moves.reframe: Meeting the rubric is necessary but not sufficient — the real question is: who outside your immediate team knows your name and impact, and could advocate for you in a 30-minute panel?
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Surfaces the hidden visibility variable that most PMs ignore — converts a checklist mentality into a relationship and influence-building problem
reframing_moves.example_language: 出了你这个小团队别人都不了解你，在升职答辩的时候，怎么能够在几十分钟的时候就展现清楚呢 — If no one outside your small team knows you, how can you make your case clear in a promotion panel that lasts only a few dozen minutes?
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_产品经理应该如何进行职业规划.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: How do I advance my career as a PM? What should I be doing?
reframing_moves.reframe: Stop asking what to do and start auditing whether you've hit the actual milestone for your current stage. 80%+ of PMs haven't — so the question isn't 'what's next' but 'have I actually completed this stage, and if not, what's blocking me from acquiring the ownership I need?'
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts from a forward-looking tactical question (what to do next) to a diagnostic backward-looking question (have I earned the right to move on). This exposes the real problem — lack of ownership scope — which is actionable, versus vague career anxiety which is not
reframing_moves.example_language: '80%以上的人都在这个思路之外，因为到了2年、3年、5年的经验，大部分人都没有达成阶段性目标' — more than 80% of people are outside this ideal path because most have not hit the stage milestones
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_产品经理的职业生涯规划是怎么样的.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Should I choose the management track or the specialist track for my career?
reframing_moves.reframe: Before asking which track to choose, ask: do you prefer spending energy understanding and influencing people, or going deep on product problems? The answer should drive the choice — not external prestige signals
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Grounds an abstract career strategy question in a concrete, answerable introspective question; de-escalates the status anxiety around management by centering personal fit instead
reframing_moves.example_language: 你是更喜欢与人打交道，察言观色，揣摩人性，还是更喜欢研究产品，沉浸其中，寻找创新
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_产品经理要如何晋升_有哪些晋升路径.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: 35-year-old PM asking: what are the 'exit options' for someone like me?
reframing_moves.reframe: The real question is not what exit options exist, but what is your current capability profile — and which of the four paths (large company management, small company leadership, business unit GM, entrepreneurship/VC) does your specific profile best match?
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Prevents the poster from treating all paths as equally available regardless of preparation; forces a capability self-assessment before path selection, which is the correct sequencing
reframing_moves.example_language: The answer maps out four distinct paths and assigns rough probabilities (30%/30%/20%/10%) — signaling that path availability is not random but correlated with what you've built
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_那些35岁以上的产品经理都去做什么了.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: My career is about choosing the right companies to work for
reframing_moves.reframe: Your career is about managing your personal brand — every departure, every transition, and every role is a visible data point in a transparent industry
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Expands the time horizon and the audience; shifts from transactional ('get a job') to reputational ('build a track record') thinking
reframing_moves.example_language: 互联网的最大特性就是'透明'，你是好的臭不了，你真搞臭了也遮不住 (The internet's defining feature is transparency — you can't hide quality, and you can't hide damage)
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_互联网人跳槽的注意事项有哪些.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I always feel like I could have answered better in the defense after the fact — I keep missing my chance
reframing_moves.reframe: No one achieves their ideal defense performance in the moment; the standard isn't perfection, it's continuous improvement across attempts
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Normalizes the performance gap as universal rather than personal; reorients the retrospective from a self-judgment exercise to a development input for the next attempt
reframing_moves.example_language: 很少有人能做到真正完美的答辩表现，每一次都比上一次做到更好就足够了

reframing_moves.original_framing: I have a product director title at a mid-size company — am I a senior PM?
reframing_moves.reframe: The title doesn't tell you anything. The real question is: are you the autonomous decision-maker for a business with real P&L consequence, or are you an executor with a senior label?
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Decouples seniority from title and re-anchors it to accountability and autonomy — which are the actual market-facing signals that determine comp and external opportunity
reframing_moves.example_language: Tencent reportedly stripped the PM title from everyone below level 12 because only those who 'independently own a complete business with resource and decision authority' qualify as product managers in the real sense
